description:
CAPABILITY CANDIDATE for scripts/test-doctor.py --mock-drift. Found 2026-10-07 while walking the slow-marked test set. Not built — needs a go-ahead (it extends a shipped tool, so it is a change to production tooling rather than a test fix).

WHY: the detector answers ONE question — "does patching this target move the attribute the code reads?" That caught a real case today (test_infer_router patched domain.models._internal.provider.get_provider while infer.py does `from domain.models import get_provider`; the tool printed `fix: patch("domain.models.get_provider")` and exited 1, independently matching what I derived by hand).

But packages/core-py/tests/test_process_isolation.py died 8x with a defect that question cannot reach: the fixture's `monkeypatch.setattr(mw_mod, "_slo_worker_main", _fake_slo_worker_main)` patches the EXACT module production reads, so the binding moves and condition (1) is satisfied — but ProcessGuard's default flipped from SUBPROCESS to THREAD (b002cc789, an unrelated commit), so nothing ever routes through that symbol. A perfect patch aimed at a symbol that exists, on a seam production no longer uses.

THREE GAPS, in order of value:

1. SCAN monkeypatch.setattr too. --mock-drift only enumerates patch("string") targets, so this fixture's target was never a candidate at all. Both spellings are patching; the detector should see both.

2. BOOM-VS-BASELINE for suspects. Today a suspect that passes with the seam booby-trapped is "harmless". A suspect that FAILS THE SAME WAY with and without the boom is neither harmless nor confirmed — it is an unrelated failure sitting next to a dead seam. That case currently falls through both labels. Compare boom run against baseline run instead of classifying on pass/fail alone.

3. FAIL-FIRST TRIAGE for the slow set. Static drift analysis found 0 of the 11 failures in this file; the run itself named every seam worth checking. Cheapest useful step is to run the deselected set and let failures point.

DETECTOR IS NOT AT FAULT FOR MISSING #3 — it diagnoses bindings, and every binding involved was correct. This is a different question (call path, not binding) and deserves a separate answer rather than being folded into --mock-drift's exit code.

RELATED: card 33773fce-b (refactor-drift backlog, ~300 of 619 failures) — the failures above are the same species: tests reading a pre-refactor API. Evidence + analysis in ~/.config/dev-notes/2026-10-05-mock-target-shim-drift.md, Round 6.

LANDED `c1308c9c9` (branch feat/mock-drift-dead-seam), merged into fix/db-pool-root-and-download-progress as `32005e630`.

1. Spellings unified — `monkeypatch.setattr("a.b.c", …)` is now scanned beside
   `patch("a.b.c")`: 166 -> 203 targets (+37 real ones). The 1064 object-form
   sites name no dotted path, so they are out of scope by construction.
2. `--dead-seam <file>` — the boom-vs-baseline probe. `--mock-drift` asks
   "does the patch move the binding?" and counts yes as OK; that is a statement
   about *binding*, not *execution*, so a patch aimed at a symbol production
   never routes through passes every static condition while proving nothing.
   The probe runs the test twice (baseline, then with that symbol replaced by
   a raiser) and reports dead only when the boom never fires.
   scripts/dead_seam_plugin.py carries the boom half; the marker travels to a
   FILE so pytest capture cannot turn an armed run into an unarmed one.

GUARD: the probe's own dangerous failure mode is the mirror of the detector's —
calling a LIVE seam dead would get a working mock deleted. Non-callable /
unresolvable symbols write not-probeable/unresolved -> inconclusive, never
dead; pytest rc 4/5 -> inconclusive; a red baseline skips the 2nd run.

FIRST FIND (real, pre-existing): tests/test_knowledge_augmenter.py patches
domain.learner...knowledge_augmenter.get_knowledge_memory while production reads
it from domain.knowledge / domain.memory. --mock-drift went from "no drift"
(rc 0) to 2 confirmed; --dead-seam confirms the mock never executes.

GATES: tests/test_doctor_mock_drift.py 46 passed (was 24); ruff check + format
clean; mypy 0 new (1 pre-existing AST.lineno); tool runtime 15.68s -> 11.75s
(within noise on a loaded box).
title: --mock-drift: scan monkeypatch.setattr + boom-vs-baseline probe (dead-seam class)

description:
REPORT ONLY — found 2026-10-07. The AttributeError on this endpoint was fixed and committed (64820c3aa, user-approved): FeedbackController now defines feedback_dir = repo_root/"data", so /training/export-text returns 200 instead of 500. THIS card is about what the 200 now contains.

WHAT: the endpoint returns 200 with pairs_count: 0, always.

WHY: it reads repo_root/"data/feedback.jsonl". That file does not exist anywhere in the main tree — training/feeds.py:34 and domain/training/_internal/experience_adapter.py:71 point at the same path, but nothing writes it. So the endpoint is hollow-but-correct: no crash, no data.

THE MISMATCH: FeedbackController was migrated to MogDB — its own docstring says "instead of raw JSON/JSONL" — and record_feedback() stores exactly the three fields this endpoint filters on (user_message, assistant_response, quality) into a MogDB collection. The export endpoint was never migrated with it. It still reads a JSONL file that the new storage path stopped writing.

So the data exists; the reader points at the old medium.

FIX: read the collection instead of the file. Small, but it changes what the endpoint returns (0 -> real pairs), so it needs a call rather than a drive-by.

CONSEQUENCE IF IGNORED: the UI silently shows "no pairs to export" forever while pairs accumulate in MogDB. A zero that looks like a legitimate empty state is worse than an error — nothing fails, so nothing gets reported.

EVIDENCE: tests/test_feedback_system.py::test_export_training now asserts the real contract (file key, target_count) and passes with pairs_count 0. If the endpoint is migrated, that assertion may need to widen to accept a non-zero count.

RELATED: card e205b15c and db9c4e70 are the other two findings from the same slow-test march. Notes in ~/.config/dev-notes/2026-10-05-mock-target-shim-drift.md, Round 4.
title: /training/export-text returns 200 with pairs_count always 0 — export never migrated to MogDB

description:
Symptom: running `test_shell_repl_more.py` together with eight sibling files
reports **86** failures; running it alone reports **85**, at both baseline and
HEAD. The single differing test is `TestModuleHelpers::test_color_with_no_color_env`,
which fails at `tests/test_shell_repl_more.py:874` with
`assert False is True  where False = repl_mod._COLOR_ENABLED`.

Root cause — two lines that never see each other:

    packages/core-py/tests/test_console.py:16   os.environ["NO_COLOR"] = "1"
    domain/shell/_internal/repl.py:110          _COLOR_ENABLED = not os.environ.get("NO_COLOR")

`test_console.py` writes `NO_COLOR` at module import and never restores it, so
it leaks process-wide. The colour test then does `importlib.reload(repl_mod)`
after its own `patch.dict` exits and expects `_COLOR_ENABLED is True` — but the
ambient env still has `NO_COLOR=1` from the earlier file, so the reload computes
False. Colour is decided once at import, making the test an ambient-env test in
a shared process.

Confirmed not a caret regression: solo at HEAD the test **passes in 1.25s**,
`repl.py` is untouched by that campaign, and `test_shell_repl_more.py` contains
zero `TuiRepl(` constructions and zero `_main`/`read_key` references.

Fix (test-side, not product-side): replace the module-level assignment with a
scoped `patch.dict(os.environ, ...)` and a `request.addfinalizer`/teardown that
restores the previous value, or set the variable only inside the tests that
need it. If colour must be tested after reload, assert against the env rather
than the reloaded constant.

Found by the caret campaign's P5 verify pass
(`packages/core-py/tests/test_caret_invariants.py`), recorded so the next
multi-file run does not re-derive it.
title: Restore NO_COLOR after test_console import (cross-file env pollution)

description:
GOAL: one test folder. Tests currently live in 4 roots + 11 package dirs, and 86 test basenames are duplicated repo-wide (documented in packages/core-py/pytest.ini, worked around with --import-mode=importlib rather than fixed).

=== CURRENT STATE (measured 2026-10-08) ===
  packages/core-py/tests    798 files / 43,412 test fns   COLLECTED
  tests/                    144 files /  3,587 test fns   COLLECTED
  apps/cli/tests             24 files /    430 test fns   COLLECTED
  apps/api/server/tests      96 files /  1,418 test fns   ORPHANED (not in testpaths)
  packages/*/tests          11 dirs (aml, app-planner, avion, bawl, chargectl,
                              downcraft, infra-lib, mogdb, sdk-py, ...)
  Total in 4 roots: 1,062 files

=== USER DECISIONS (2026-10-08) ===
1. Canonical folder = REPO-ROOT tests/ (literal single folder).
2. Diverged duplicate pairs = REPORT ONLY, do not merge yet.

=== KNOWN RISKS (from the repo's own docs) ===
- pytest.ini header: pytest picks ONE configfile = nearest ini to the common
  ancestor of the args. A root-level arg moves rootdir to the repo root and
  stops the inner ini applying -> mogdb/chargectl fall off sys.path and
  collection ABORTS. Both pytest.ini files exist to prevent this.
- packages/core-py/pytest.ini must stay in sync or "a drift here is invisible
  from the repo root."
- conftest.py files use Path(__file__) parent arithmetic:
    tests/conftest.py:10            _REPO_ROOT = .parent.parent
    packages/core-py/tests:14       parents[2]  (-> breaks if depth changes)
    apps/cli/tests:10               ../src      (-> breaks if moved)
  These MUST be recalculated after the move or sys.path silently loses entries.
- --import-mode=importlib is already set; it was the workaround for the
  duplicate-basename problem and can be revisited once deduped.

=== PLAN ===
1. git mv the 3 non-canonical roots under tests/ with DISTINCT subdirs:
     packages/core-py/tests -> tests/core-py/
     apps/cli/tests         -> tests/cli/
     apps/api/server/tests  -> tests/api-server/
   (distinct subdirs so the 37 colliding router basenames cannot overwrite)
2. Recalculate every conftest path expression for the new depth.
3. pytest.ini: testpaths = tests ; keep pythonpath keys intact.
4. Repoint or retire packages/core-py/pytest.ini (its testpaths=tests would
   otherwise collect nothing).
5. REPORT the diverged duplicate pairs (37 router files; 0 identical /
   25 diverged among the orphaned) - no merging.
6. Verify: collection count before == after; full suite green-or-same.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
- exactly ONE collected test root
- no test basename appears in two collected locations
- collected test count matches pre-move (no silent drops)
title: single test root: consolidate 4 test folders into repo-root tests/

description:
Discovered while root-causing b015795b (fixed there for useChatModelSettings only).

Two verified mechanisms, both cross-file:

1. SHARED KV. apps/web tests share one chatDB KV store. Probed: file A does
   chatDB.setKV('app-settings', {defaultTemp: 999}) and file B reads 999.
   Any test that calls the real store's updateSettings() therefore persists
   settings that EVERY later test file hydrates.

2. ASYNC HYDRATION. lib/store.ts:168 kicks off initStore() at module import;
   it reads that KV and setState()s whenever the read resolves. Unawaited, it
   lands AFTER a test's beforeEach reset and re-poisons defaultTemp — the
   hook's store-sync effect then applies the leaked value over the value the
   test just fetched (symptom: "expected 0.8 to be 0.5").

3. LIVE BACKEND WRITES. updateSettings → _pushToBackend →
   settingsController.updateGeneration PATCHes http://localhost:8000/settings/
   generation. Before the fix, useChatModelSettings made 6 such calls per run —
   mutating whatever backend happened to be up, including another session's.

Files touching the store, still unprotected (no @/lib/settings-controller mock):
  components/CommandPalette.test.tsx
  features/chat/ChatPage.test.tsx
  features/chat/components/input/VoiceSettingsPanel.test.tsx
  features/chat/hooks/useVoiceChat.test.ts
(store.test.ts / store.migration.test.ts test the store itself and already mock chatDB.)

Fix pattern (proven in useChatModelSettings.test.ts):
  beforeEach(async () => { await initStore(); ...reset to DEFAULT_SETTINGS... })
  vi.mock('@/lib/settings-controller', ...)
  hard guard: spyOn(globalThis,'fetch') asserted empty in afterEach.

Sweep method: run each file and grep for localhost:8000 calls, or add the
fetch guard and read the offending URLs.

Follow-up worth considering: make the KV per-file (or have tests mock
@/lib/db) so this class cannot recur file-by-file.
title: Tests share one app-settings KV and write to the live backend (4 unprotected files)

description:
The campaign's last open half, named by `Caret`'s own docstring:

    `tui_repl` kept its own `_input_buf` and `_input_cursor` for 28 more and
    called `_filter_key` not at all, so Ctrl+W was decided twice for one
    keystroke

P4 closed the *dispatch* half (one `Caret.claims(key)` branch) but left the
*state* half: `TuiRepl.__init__` still declares two fields, and every keystroke
builds a throwaway `Caret` from them at `tui_repl.py:1744`:

    line = Caret("".join(self._input_buf), self._input_cursor)
    if line.apply(key):
        self._input_buf = line.buf
    self._input_cursor = line.caret

So the type exists, is constructed and torn down on the hot path, and the pair
sitting beside it is never made one. Two independently-assigned fields can be
set out of step — a caret that indexes past its buffer is representable —
which is exactly the state `Caret`'s clamping setter exists to make
unrepresentable.

Scope (approved: full rename + the existing-test edits that follow from it):

1. `TuiRepl.__init__` holds `self._input: Caret`; the two fields disappear.
2. All 62 production sites become `self._input.buf` / `self._input.caret`.
   The two truthiness sites (1655, 1709) must read `not self._input.buf` —
   `Caret` has no `__bool__`, so `not self._input` is unconditionally False
   and would silently break "press / at an empty prompt to search".
3. The `getattr(self, "_input_buf", [])` defensiveness at 1007 goes: every
   fixture constructs via `TuiRepl(...)`, so `_input` always exists.
4. The per-keystroke bridge collapses to `self._input.apply(key)`.
5. `Caret.buf` gains a clamping setter so rebinding the buffer re-clamps the
   index. Nothing rebinds `.buf` in production today, so this is inert for the
   21 widget boxes — but it is the mechanism P6 relies on, and it makes the
   class's own claim ("the bad state is never representable") true for the
   first time. `__slots__` moves `buf` -> `_buf`; no test asserts `__slots__`.
6. The 228 existing test lines across 5 files rename to `.buf`/`.caret` —
   all mechanical, none rewritten in what they assert.
7. `test_caret_invariants._DEFERRED` drops `_input_cursor` deliberately: it
   asserted the deferral, and P6 is the event it said would have to update it.

Acceptance (baseline -> target): `_input_buf|_input_cursor` in domain/+apps/
**63 -> 0**; `Caret(` constructions inside `TuiRepl._main` **1 -> 0**; the
invariant guard 8/8 green with `_DEFERRED` updated; the 9-file gate 0 new
failures (85 `repl_more` baseline unchanged); ruff 0 -> 0; 4 benchmarks exit 0
with no >2% regression; TDD red proven first on the structural assertion
("tui_repl still keeps its own (buf, caret) pair").

Shared-workspace acceptance: no new package/app/doc, so no index entry is owed
(`Caret` and `TuiRepl` are existing files); no new venv/node_modules/lockfile —
the pinned interpreter and root toolchain are reused. Coordination: continuation
of `feat/caret-core` (P1-P5 landed on it); no other session owns
`domain/shell/_internal/`. Approved by the user as the full rename.
title: TUI: caret core P6 — the REPL input line stops keeping its own (buf, caret) pair

description:
DEFECT (destructive test fixture) — found 2026-10-08 while consolidating test roots.

FILE: tests/api-server/test_files_router.py  (was apps/api/server/tests/test_files_router.py)

The autouse fixture `_cleanup_uploads` targets the REAL stores on every teardown:

    @pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
    def _cleanup_uploads():
        yield
        db = _get_db()
        db.collection("files").delete_many({})          # wipes the ENTIRE uploads DB
        for f in _upload_dir.iterdir():
            if f.is_file(): f.unlink(missing_ok=True)   # deletes EVERY file in data/uploads/

WHY IT MATTERS
- `_upload_dir = FilesRouter().UPLOADS_DIR` -> repo data/uploads (real user files)
- `_get_db()` -> get_db("uploads_mogdb") -> the real uploads database
- It has run against live data repeatedly. Journal replay shows 537 metadata
  records destroyed in a single wipe: 536 were test debris rebuilt by prior runs,
  but 1791188358_nbaallelo_csv.csv (18,173,265 bytes) was a REAL user upload.
- data/uploads_json/files.json was reduced to 2 bytes.

EVIDENCE
- journal (append-only) preserves the insert at line 3498:
  {"op":"insert","data":{"file_id":"1791188358_nbaallelo_csv",
   "filename":"1791188358_nbaallelo_csv.csv","original_name":"nbaallelo.csv",
   "size_bytes":18173265,...}}
- wipe op at line 3611: {"op":"delete_many","data":{"query":{},"count":2}}
- original bytes survive intact at runs/downloads/nbaallelo.csv (exact size match)

ROOT CAUSE
Test isolation: the fixture clears shared mutable state instead of creating
private state. Compare with the repo convention of tmp_path/monkeypatch.

REQUIRED FIX (not applied — awaiting owner)
- monkeypatch FilesRouter.UPLOADS_DIR to tmp_path

description:
Symptom: `repl._cmd_tui()` never returns when stdin is at EOF (a closed pipe,
or `/dev/null` under a background run). One core is pinned and the process is
unkillable-by-timeout unless the suite passes one.

Chain, each step reproduced:

    _cmd_tui -> TuiRepl.run() -> _main
      key = self._session.read_key(timeout=0.1)      tui_repl.py:1489
        select.select([self.fd], [], [], timeout)    tui_session.py:878

`select` reports EOF as *always readable*, so it returns instantly instead of
waiting out the 0.1s; `read_key` then yields no usable key and `_main` neither
quits nor sleeps. The loop is therefore a tight spin, not a poll.

Two independent defects sit behind the three TUI tests that hang. A fourth
baseline timeout, `TestCmdLogsExplainV2::test_logs_follow`, hangs in a
*different* loop (`/logs --follow`) with the same missing-EOF-guard shape —
related, but not this chain, so it is noted here rather than folded into a/b.

1. **No EOF guard in the key loop (production).** `read_key` has no way to
   report "the stream ended", so `_main` cannot break out. Probed directly:
   `select([fd0], 0.1s) -> [0] after 0.0000s` — the requested 0.1s is never
   paid, so the loop has no throttle at all. This is the real bug: the TUI is
   a busy-wait the moment its input closes.

2. **`test_tui_runtime_error` has never tested what it names (test).** It
   patches `builtins.__import__` for the *fully qualified* name
   `domain.shell._internal.tui_repl`, but `_cmd_tui` uses a relative import:

       from .tui_repl import TuiRepl

   which calls `__import__('tui_repl', level=1)`. The name never matches, so
   the mock never fires (standalone probe: `patch fired: False`) and the test
   drives the **real** TuiRepl. It passes only because the real TUI happens to
   raise; against a working TUI it hangs. `TestCmdTuiExtra::test_tui` applies
   no patch at all and hangs the same way.

Evidence it is pre-existing, not introduced by the caret campaign: the P5
baseline `.splitwork/p5_gate.log` already carries four
`Failed: Timeout (>180.0s) from pytest-timeout` entries — three from this
chain (`TestCmdTui::test_tui_runtime_error`,
`TestCmdTuiDeeper2::test_tui_runtime_error`, `TestCmdTuiExtra::test_tui`) and
one from `TestCmdLogsExplainV2::test_logs_follow`. Earlier runs passed
`--timeout=180`; a run without a timeout flag does not fail, it hangs.

Proposed fix (needs approval — production code):

  a. have `read_key` distinguish EOF from "no key yet" (a sentinel or a
     raised StopIteration), and let `_main` break its loop on it — the loop
     must not be able to spin without sleeping. This is what clears
     `TestCmdTuiExtra::test_tui`, which applies no patch at all.
  b. repoint the two `test_tui_runtime_error` patches at
     `domain.shell._internal.tui_repl.TuiRepl`. Patching
     `domain.shell._internal.repl.TuiRepl` is *not* an option: `_cmd_tui`
     imports inside the function, so that module never gains a `TuiRepl`
     attribute to patch (probe: `UNPATCHABLE — has no such attribute`), while
     patching the source module binds the mock (`hit (mock bound) OK`).
  c. keep `--timeout` on any suite invocation, since nothing else stops this.

Coordination: discovered while gating P6 (card 7781dfe5), which does not touch
the key loop's EOF behaviour — P6 replaces the pair with one `Caret` and stops
at `self._input.apply(key)`. No other session owns `domain/shell/_internal/`.
Shared-workspace acceptance: no new package/app/doc, no new venv or lockfile.
title: TUI: _main key loop busy-spins at 100% CPU when stdin reaches EOF

DISCOVERY from the card d4cdfb0d live demo: DownloadsCard showed '14.0 KB / 78.0 KB' for a completed 79872 B external download. Root cause in ExternalDownloadBackend.download()'s plain (compressed=False) path: _progress(len(chunk), file_size) is called with the CURRENT CHUNK size, and the closure computes current = bytes_done + bytes_written where bytes_done only increments AFTER the file finishes (bytes_done += file_size) — so during the transfer the registry sees 8192/16384/... (last chunk, resets per file) instead of cumulative bytes; 65536+14336 chunks -> final report 14336. Percentage is wrong mid-transfer too (it only looks right because completion forces 100.0). The compressed path is unaffected if CompressedDownloader reports cumulative written bytes (verify first). Fix: track file_bytes += len(chunk) per file and pass that to _progress; add a progress-accounting test to tests/core-py/test_external_download.py (owner's file — coordinate). Surfaced only once download_with made the route actually run.
PICKED UP (2026-10-09): base = feat/download-contract-generic tip (9bccbdce7) — my own download stack, so the uncommitted rename copies in shared stay the source of truth and the fix lands on the stack it belongs to. Fix = cumulative file_bytes per chunk in the plain path; verify the compressed path; progress-accounting test (test_external_download.py ownership checked first).
SHIPPED 2026-10-09 commit 8cd52de8c on fix/download-progress-accounting (stacked on feat/download-contract-generic 9bccbdce7), pushed to origin. Plain path now tracks file_bytes += len(chunk) and passes the running per-file total; the closure adds bytes_done so callers see a running total within AND across files. Compressed path VERIFIED cumulative (compressed_transfer.py uncompressed_size accumulator) — untouched, as the card directed. New tests/core-py/test_external_download.py: deterministic fake-urlopen harness (fixed chunk schedule 65536/65536/1000, SLO_CACHE_DIR tmp isolation, try_register stubbed) pinning the exact cumulative sequence [65536, 131072, 132072] across two files + grand-total denominator + monotonicity. GREEN: worktree 20 passed; SHARED full download surface 117 passed (manager+seam+external+git+local); ruff + py_compile clean; shared synced 2/2 byte-identical (M coordination copies). Note: commit initially landed on feat/download-contract-generic (worktree branch) — split to its own stacked branch; contract branch rewound to what origin already had (no force-push).

description:
Symptom: `TestCmdLogsExplainV2::test_logs_follow` hits `pytest-timeout` on
every run. It is one of the four timeouts the P5 baseline already recorded as
`Timeout (>180.0s)`, so it is pre-existing rather than introduced by the caret
campaign.

The loop, in full (`repl.py`, `_cmd_logs`):

    if follow:
        self._print(f"  {_C_DIM}Following — press Ctrl+C to stop{_C_RESET}")
        try:
            offset = len(self._log_buffer)
            while True:
                time.sleep(0.5)
                new_entries = self._log_buffer.get(..., offset=offset)
                for e in new_entries:
                    self._print(self._log_display._format_entry(e))
                offset += len(new_entries)
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            self._print()

`while True` with `KeyboardInterrupt` as the *only* exit. Three things follow:

1. **It is not a CPU spin.** Unlike the TUI key loop — where `select` reports a
   closed descriptor readable in 0.0000s and the requested 0.1 s is never paid —
   this sleeps 0.5 s per iteration. It burns no core; it just never finishes.
   Calling both "the same missing-EOF-guard shape" is right about the cause and
   wrong about the symptom, which is why they are separate cards.

2. **A closed stdin cannot stop it.** `KeyboardInterrupt` arrives from a signal
   on a real terminal. Under a background run stdin is already at EOF, so no key
   ever arrives to turn into Ctrl+C, and nothing else in the loop checks whether
   the session should still be following.

3. **The test has no way to win.** It cannot inject the one condition the loop
   exits on, so the only outcome available is `--timeout`.

Why this needs a decision rather than a patch: "when should `--follow` stop?" is
a product question with at least three defensible answers, and they differ in
what the operator sees —

  a. stop when the input descriptor reaches EOF (same rule `_main` now uses);
  b. stop after a bounded number of idle polls, or on an explicit `--follow-timeout`;
  c. keep running forever, and fix the *test* to drive the loop through a
     bounded iterator instead of the production command.

(c) is the only one that changes nothing in production, and it is the one I would
want confirmed: the loop's current behaviour is defensible for an interactive
shell — "follow until Ctrl+C" is what the help text promises — so this may be a
test-shape bug rather than a product bug.

Coordination: split out of card `8447a953` (TUI EOF spin) when that card's
production fix landed, so the two mechanisms do not get closed as one. No other
session owns `domain/shell/_internal/repl.py`. Shared-workspace acceptance: no
new package/app/doc, no new venv or lockfile.
title: shell: `/logs --follow` has no exit condition, so it never returns

blocked on an inherited futex. This is the card 075 mechanism, made visible.

SPAWN CADENCE (wave starts, seconds of etimes at observation)
    3044 x7 | 2443 x7 | 1843 x5 | 1243 | 643 | 43
=> a new child appears roughly every 600s, which is exactly --timeout=600.
Their log shows 11 "Timeout" banners, so each timeout leaves one more
futex-blocked orphan behind.

RESOURCE IMPACT (why concurrent runs in this worktree slow down)
    free: 23Gi total, 9.0Gi used, Swap 2.0Gi used of 3.8Gi
    load average 3.40 on 8 cores -> NOT CPU-bound; it is process + swap
    pressure. Each child holds a COW copy of the parent heap (5.4% each).

WHERE IT COMES FROM
    grep -rln "os.fork()" tests/core-py/ --include="test_*.py"
      -> tests/core-py/test_pugqeep_process_mgmt.py   (ONLY such file)

REPRO / NON-REPRO
- isolated: pytest tests/core-py/test_pugqeep_process_mgmt.py
  -> 175 passed in 48s, exit 0. Matches the card "file-alone + pair runs pass".
- full group: the leak appears. So the fork deadlocks only when the parent is
  concurrently busy or killed, not when it runs alone.

CAUTION
Do NOT kill these children to clean up: they belong to another sessions live
run, and killing them would corrupt that gate. Left untouched here.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION (for the card owner, not done here)
- make the forked child close or reinit inherited sync primitives after fork
  (atfork handler, or a bare exec), and/or
- reap children in the test teardown, and/or
- have pytest-timeout kill the process group, not just the test thread.
title: fork-futex leak forensics (evidence for card 32914d93): 24 idle children, futex_do_wait, 2Gi swap

description:
ROOT-CAUSED HANG — this is what killed the original C3 chunk (o-w) of the
full-suite run (card vq-huffm), and it is a DIFFERENT hanger from card
32914d93 (which blames test_pugqeep_process_mgmt / fork futex).

SYMPTOM
  Chunk C3 (tests/core-py/test_[o-w]*) hit the shell timeout: exit=124 at
  timeout 3000, only 41% rendered, no pytest summary line. -q mode means the
  failure summary is only written at exit, so that whole 50-minute run was
  unrecoverable.
  Reproduced on a retry: C3b (sa-sh) froze with zero byte growth for 60s+
  on exactly one test, no status emitted:

    tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py::TestCmdLogsExplainV2::test_logs_follow

  Had to SIGTERM it manually (exit=143).

ROOT CAUSE — an unguarded duplicate of a guarded test
  There are THREE test_logs_follow definitions in
  tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py:

    line  8330  class TestCmdLogsLevels      has_alarm=2   <- GUARDED, never hangs
    line 20305  class TestCmdLogsExplainV2   has_alarm=0   <- HANGS
    line 23086  class TestCmdLogsDeeperV2    has_alarm=0   <- calls "follow 1", bounded

  The guarded copy (8330) reads:

      # Follow mode has a while True loop - just test it doesn't crash on init
      def alarm_handler(signum, frame):
          raise KeyboardInterrupt()
      old_handler = signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, alarm_handler)
      signal.alarm(1)
      try:
          repl._cmd_logs("-f")
      except KeyboardInterrupt:
          pass
      finally:
          signal.alarm(0)
          signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, old_handler)

  The hanging copy (20305) has NO alarm, NO KeyboardInterrupt handler:

      def test_logs_follow(self, repl):
          repl._log_buffer.clear()
          _run_with_io(repl, [], lambda: repl._cmd_logs("-f"))
          assert repl._last_exit_code == 0

  Production side: domain/shell/_internal/repl.py
      2536: def _cmd_logs(self, args: str = "") -> None:
      2720:     while True:        <- the follow-mode loop

  So the test enters repl.py:2720's while True with a cleared log buffer and
  nothing ever breaks the loop. The 8330 copy breaks it with SIGALRM; 20305
  never can -> blocks forever.

WHY IT SLIPPED THROUGH
  - file-alone and pair runs pass, because alphabetical/pytest ordering does
    not always reach this class before other work (same shape as 32914d93's
    "file-alone + pair runs pass").
  - -m "not slow" deselects slow tests but this is an infinite loop, not a
    slow test, so the marker never applies.

SUGGESTED FIX (NOT APPLIED — needs approval, file may be owned elsewhere)
  Mirror the 8330 guard into 20305: install a SIGALRM handler that raises
  KeyboardInterrupt, signal.alarm(1) around the _cmd_logs("-f") call, then
  always signal.alarm(0) + restore the previous handler in finally.
  Also review 23086 (TestCmdLogsDeeperV2) — unguarded too, though it passes
  "follow 1" which appears bounded; unverified whether it can hang.

WORKAROUND ALREADY IN USE (mine, no code change)
  Re-run that one file with a deselect so coverage completes:

    pytest tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py \
      --deselect tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py::TestCmdLogsExplainV2::test_logs_follow

PROCESS NOTE FOR FUTURE RUNS
  Switched all remaining chunks to verbose + PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 streaming.
  Verbose writes one line per test AS IT COMPLETES, so a killed run still
  yields every completed result (this is how 4149 results were salvaged from
  the killed C3b). With -q, a timeout discards everything — do not use -q for
  long chunks.
title: HANG: test_shell_repl_more TestCmdLogsExplainV2::test_logs_follow blocks forever (unguarded _cmd_logs -f while True) - killed C3 chunk

description:
ORDER-DEPENDENT TEST ISOLATION DEFECT — reproduced on demand, not a product bug.

SYMPTOM (seen in chunk C3a of the full-suite run, card vq-huffm)
  tests/core-py/test_quantized_matmul.py:
      TestQuantine::test_init_symmetric
      TestQuantine::test_init_asymmetric
      TestQuantizeStateDict::test_returns_tensor_info

  The assertion is self-contradictory on its face:

    AssertionError: assert <QuantMode.SYMMETRIC: 'symmetric'> == <QuantMode.SYMMETRIC: 'symmetric'>
      +  where <QuantMode.SYMMETRIC> = <domain...quantization.Quantine object>._mode
      +  and   <QuantMode.SYMMETRIC> = QuantMode.SYMMETRIC

  Two visually identical enum members failing == means they are TWO DIFFERENT
  class objects — Python Enum does not define __eq__, so it is identity-based.

REPRODUCTION (2 seconds, deterministic)
  pytest tests/core-py/test_quantized_matmul.py -q
      -> 3 passed                       (passes alone)

  pytest tests/core-py/test_quantization_coverage.py \
         <the 3 tests above> -q
      -> 3 failed, 31 passed            (fails)

  So the failure depends entirely on test_quantization_coverage.py running first.

ROOT CAUSE
  tests/core-py/test_quantization_coverage.py calls importlib.reload():
      line 106:  importlib.reload(q)
      line 114:  importlib.reload(q)

  reload() re-executes the module in the EXISTING module object, which
  re-creates the QuantMode Enum class — a brand-new class object.

  Collection order (glob/locale order in tests/core-py/):
      5  test_quantization_coverage.py   <- reload() runs here
      9  test_quantized_matmul.py        <- holds the OLD QuantMode binding

  test_quantized_matmul.py binds QuantMode AT COLLECTION TIME (module-level
  import). The reload then swaps in a new QuantMode. When the matmul tests
  later construct a Quantine, engine._mode is a member of the NEW class while
  the test compares against the OLD class -> identity mismatch -> assert fails,
  even though both render as QuantMode.SYMMETRIC.

WHY IT IS EASY TO MISS
  - passes when the file runs alone (the usual local workflow)
  - only fails in a full-scope run, where files execute in collection order
  - the repr is identical on both sides, so the failure looks impossible

SUGGESTED FIXES (NOT APPLIED — needs approval)
  Preferred (fix the polluter): in test_quantization_coverage.py, make the
  reload harmless — either
    (a) capture module state and restore it in a fixture finalizer, or
    (b) reload inside a fixture that re-imports the names the other tests
        depend on, or
    (c) stop reloading entirely if the reload only exists to pick up a
        monkeypatched value — monkeypatch the attribute instead of the module.
  Alternative (defend the victim): have test_quantized_matmul.py resolve
  QuantMode lazily inside each test (module attr lookup at call time) instead
  of holding a module-level binding.

  Note: this is one instance of a wider pattern — the repo has 13 test files
  using importlib.reload / sys.modules[...] mutation. Any of them can cause
  the same class of order-dependent failure. A targeted sweep would be a
  separate, larger piece of work.

RELATED
  - The traceback for these failures shows a path that no longer exists
    (packages/core-py/tests/...) — that is a SEPARATE issue, stale .pyc with
    pre-move co_filename, card 9dba061c. Clearing bytecode does NOT fix this
    failure: verified by re-running with PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX set to a fresh
    directory (forces full recompilation) — the 3 tests still fail, while
    test_list_cached_models_includes_local_cache still fails for the unrelated
    reason that the Qwen model.slnc is absent from ~/.cache/huggingface.
title: ORDER-DEPENDENT: importlib.reload in test_quantization_coverage.py breaks test_quantized_matmul (3 failures, reproduced in 2s)

description:
SECOND FORK-FUTEX HANG (family of card 32914d93), this time in
tests/core-py/test_vector_backend.py. It killed chunk C3f of the full-suite
run (card vq-huffm); 48 of its 61 files had to be re-run separately.

SYMPTOM
  Chunk C3f (tests/core-py/test_[u-w]*) froze. Output stopped after:

    tests/core-py/test_vector_backend.py::TestVectorBESimpleOps::test_silu PASSED [  9%]

  Zero byte growth across repeated 12-25s samples. Only 13 of 61 files had
  completed (385 passed, 83 failed salvaged before the kill).

PROCESS TREE AT THE STALL (the decisive evidence)
    549915  timeout 3000 python -m pytest ...
      549916  MAIN pytest          state=S  5.8% CPU  wchan=do_wait
        559953 FORKED child        state=S  0.0% CPU  wchan=futex_do_wait  age 1895s
        559889 multiprocessing resource_tracker  wchan=anon_pipe_read  age 1744s
        559954,559955,559956,559958  [python] <defunct>   <- 4 ZOMBIES

  The child at 559953 has an IDENTICAL argv to the parent — that is the
  signature of os.fork() (fork copies argv; an exec would not). It has been
  blocked on futex_do_wait with ZERO CPU time since it was created, and the
  parent is stuck in do_wait waiting for it. So the parent forked a worker,
  the worker deadlocked on an inherited futex, and the parent blocks forever.

ROOT CAUSE (fork from a multi-threaded process)
  Only one of the 13 completed files touches fork/multiprocessing at all:

    grep -cE 'os\.fork|multiprocessing|SharedMemory|Pool\(|Process\(' over the
    13 files -> test_vector_backend.py: 2, every other file: 0
    (test_user_journeys.py, which supplied 75 of the 83 failures, has 0)

  test_vector_backend.py's own docstring:
    """Tests for VectorBE compute backend with shared memory multiprocessing."""

  WHY IT PASSES ALONE BUT DEADLOCKS IN A RUN
    pytest tests/core-py/test_vector_backend.py -q
      -> 20 passed, 1 warning in 3.30s, exit 0      (verified just now)

  The preceding u-range files (browser/dashboard journey tests) leave the
  pytest process MULTI-THREADED. POSIX fork() copies only the calling thread
  into the child, but it also copies every mutex — including mutexes currently
  held by the threads that were NOT copied. The child then waits on a lock
  whose owner does not exist there -> futex_do_wait forever. In isolation the
  process has no other threads, so the fork is safe and the file passes in 3s.

  This is the classic async-signal-safety hazard that pthread_atfork() exists
  to solve. It is the same mechanism as card 32914d93 (pugqeep fork futex),
  which also "passes file-alone and in pairs" — consistent with the
  thread-count-dependent nature of the bug.

IMPACT
  - killed a 61-file chunk; required SIGKILL of the tree (549915/549916/559953)
    and manual re-run of the remaining 48 files
  - leaves a multiprocessing resource_tracker wedged on anon_pipe_read and
    orphaned <defunct> children until the tree is killed
  - same class of leak observed in ANOTHER session's run: 24-31 idle children,
    all futex_do_wait / 0 CPU / ~5.4% mem each, spawning ~every 600s
    (see card 057cab05), which drove swap to 2.0-2.2Gi of 3.8Gi

SUGGESTED FIXES (NOT APPLIED — needs approval)
  1. Prefer a safe start method: use multiprocessing.get_context("spawn") or
     "forkserver" for the shared-memory pool instead of the default "fork".
     spawn never inherits locks — this removes the hazard outright.
  2. If fork is required, register a pthread_atfork handler that locks/unlocks
     a dedicated child-side lock, or ensure all worker threads are quiesced
     (joined) before forking.
  3. Belt-and-braces: in the test's teardown, reap children and shut down the
     pool so a wedged worker cannot outlive the test.

ALSO NOTE
  The remaining 48 u/v/w files were re-run WITHOUT test_vector_backend.py
  (it is already covered by its own passing isolated run). If the suite is
  ever run as one monolithic process, this file will hang again once the
  u-range has run before it.
notes: FIX LIKELY LANDED (2026-10-11, foreman): 9bb7ca159 (card f1816d61) PORTS main's fork->forkserver fix into VectorBE — bare mp.Pool -> mp.get_context(_pool_start_method()).Pool (forkserver default, SLO_VECTOR_START_METHOD=fork escape) + resource_tracker.getfd() pre-fork, exactly killing this card's fork-into-multithreaded futex deadlock (main solved it as 72e8fae2f + a0c0561bb, cards a0ba949b/ccad389e). Full single-process core-py gate re-running from a clean worktree WITH the fix (~/.cache/foreman-20261010/f1816d61-fullgate2.log); if the v-w zone (test_vector_backend) passes in-suite, this card's DoD is met — close on that evidence.

EVIDENCE + OFFER (2026-10-11, foreman): 9bb7ca159 (the VectorBE fork->forkserver port, part of card f1816d61) almost certainly fixes this fork-futex hang. Proof from the f1816d61 zone gate: the u-z zone containing test_vector_backend.py IN-SUITE (after 60+ other test files' threads/forkserver state in the same process) completed 100% with 0 timeouts and 0 failures in that file; a live-process probe showed 0 leaked threads and children limited to the forkserver daemon + resource_tracker (no bare fork workers wedged on inherited futexes). Steady-state perf validated (matmul 22.7ms vs fork 32.6ms, softmax 4.7 vs 6.2; one-time ~1.09s cold tax). Card is mana-assigned — offering closure; mana to confirm and move to done (evidence: 9bb7ca159 + zones/zone-uz-foreground.log).

description:
Compat matrix finding (docs/VM_COMPAT.md): 4/5 third-party corpus entries die at their first forward call/jmp (asteroids_main:93, bootmine:152, nasm_tetris:58, snake_main:146). Minimal repro: `[BITS 16]
start:
 call far_fn
far_fn:
 nop` -> OverflowError. Mechanism: forward label refs resolve to placeholder 0 during emission (_parse_label pass-1 fallback), then 16-bit _emit_call/_emit_jmp (vm.py:4436/4455) do offset.to_bytes(2, "little", signed=True) with offset ~= -0x100003 -> raises; the 32-bit path masks with & 0xFFFFFFFF so it never raises — which is why cave_game ([BITS 32]) passes. Fix direction: real pass-2 label resolution before branch emission, or give the 16-bit path the same defer/mask semantics. Blocks tier-1 third-party intake (all 16-bit/default-mode sources). Evidence + harness: scripts/compat_track.py, scripts/compat/matrix.json.

DONE 2026-10-09 (branch feat/vm-asm-intake): rel16 placeholder machinery shipped — _rel16 records genuine OverflowError during passes (still emits the \x00\x00 placeholder, same size) and re-raises only after the pass loop converges, as "16-bit {what} displacement {offset} out of range (rel16 limit)"; imm16 masking at the ALU site. Tests: test_vm_assembler_emission.py::test_16bit_forward_call_jmp_with_org, ::test_16bit_real_rel16_overflow_raises_after_convergence, plus harness probe test_probe_16bit_forward_branch_now_assembles (fwd call at org 0x100000 assembles; was OverflowError). Evidence: emission suite 156 green; vm zone 3 failed (all pre-existing) / 1702 passed.
title: X86Assembler: 16-bit forward branches crash intake — pass-1 placeholder offset raises OverflowError

description:
Compat matrix finding: bweeper.asm:37 `BOARD_OFFSET equ 0x8000 + ((BOARD_TOP * 80) + BOARD_LEFT) * 2` -> ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 16. Repro: `A equ 0x8000 + 4` fails while `A equ 8 * 20` passes — the equ path attempts int(rhs, 16) on the raw string before consulting the existing _eval_expr helper (vm.py, handles 0x/0b substitution + arithmetic + parens). Fix direction: route equ evaluation through _eval_expr (likely one call-site change). Evidence: scripts/compat/matrix.json.

Tests: test_equ_hex_literal_arithmetic, test_equ_symbol_arithmetic_bweeper_pattern, harness probe test_probe_equ_hex_expression_now_assembles. bweeper now assembles past line 37.
title: X86Assembler: `equ` RHS with hex literal + arithmetic raises ValueError — _eval_expr never reached

description:
Compat matrix planned-tier row: X86CPU._raise_interrupt pushes/pops the interrupt frame even when no handler is registered — DOS-era third-party code calling BIOS video/keyboard/disk services will continue with zero effect and zero diagnostics. No corpus entry reaches runtime yet (blocked by the forward-branch + silent-directive cards), so this is static evidence; the harness interrupt-spy (compat_track.run_program) already counts unhandled vectors and will produce the runtime number when intake opens. Decision needed: minimal IVT stubs (video=write text buffer, keyboard=read queue, disk=BlockDevice) vs explicit-refuse (raise DeviceFault on unregistered INT) so programs fail loudly. Manifest: scripts/compat/manifest.json planned rows (BIOS video/keyboard/disk, real-mode IVT).
APPROACH (2026-10-09, corpus-evidence recon): DECISION — minimal IVT stubs, NOT
explicit-refuse: as-upstream execution is the tier-1 goal; the harness
interrupt-spy already provides the loud diagnostic (unhandled vector counts per
row), so refuse-everything would only fault programs we are trying to run.
Service surface sized by ACTUAL corpus call sites (grep of all corpus .asm):
INT 10h AH=00 (set mode) / 01 (cursor type) / 02 (set cursor) / 03 (get cursor) /
09 (write char+attr) / 0A (write char) / 0E (teletype) / 0F (get mode) — called
by bweeper, nasm_tetris, bootmine; INT 16h AH=00 (read key) / 01 (peek);
INT 1Ah AH=00/01 (clock). INT 13h DEFERRED: zero corpus call sites — its
disk tier gets a card when a corpus program reaches for it.
Mechanics: handlers register in X86VirtualSystem.__init__ next to INT 0x80 so
compat_track's run_program sees them with no harness change; unhandled-spy
drops 10/16/1A from every row. Video char writes land in the flat VGA text
buffer at 0xB8000 — the harness's vga_bytes_changed window, the first matrix
signal of actual rendering. CF/ZF returns patch the stacked EFLAGS at [esp+8]
(the simulated IRET in _raise_interrupt restores EFLAGS from the stack, so
in-handler flag writes alone would be clobbered). INT 16h empty queue returns
AX=0 — documented deviation from real BIOS blocking (no blocking-read tier yet;
corpus treats 0 as 'no key'); feed_key API carries test/harness input.
OUT OF SCOPE: bweeper's es=0xB000 rendering path — flat model makes es:[di]
writes land at [edi], i.e. this is SEGMENTATION, not BIOS; follow-up card.
Also: INT 21h (DOS) stays silent-unregistered (separate DOS tier).

SHIPPED (2026-10-09, branch feat/vm-bios-int): minimal IVT stubs, not
explicit-refuse (as-upstream execution is the tier-1 goal; the harness
interrupt-spy keeps the loud diagnostic). X86BiosServices registers INT
10h (AH=00/01/02/03/09/0A/0E/0F video: mode, cursor type+pos get/set,
char+attr writes, teletype with wrap, get mode), INT 16h (AH=00 read —
empty queue returns AX=0, documented deviation from real blocking — and
AH=01 peek with ZF via stacked-EFLAGS patch), INT 1Ah (AH=00/01 PIT
ticks CX:DX). Video writes land in the flat VGA text buffer at 0xB8000.
Unknown AH counted in vs._bios.unknown, not faulted. INT 13h NOT
registered (zero corpus call sites — disk tier gets its own card);
INT 21h stays silent-unregistered. VERDICT: bweeper unhandled_irqs
{'INT 0x10': 51, 'INT 0x16': 17} -> {} and vga_bytes_changed 0 -> 4000
(first rendering-tier matrix evidence); verdict stays budget.
Evidence: 17 new BIOS unit tests + 1 new compat probe test green
(30/30 with compat_track), matrix regen single-row change, cave
benchmark hud_ok=true (1246.4 ms/frame mean). One implementation bug
caught by the tests mid-build: AH=09 must walk consecutive cells
without moving the stored cursor.
title: VM runtime tier: BIOS services (INT 10h/16h/13h) absent — unregistered vectors are silent no-ops

description:
slot_history.jsonl append race: two writers read the same parent hash and both append, leaving a stale-parent node that verify reports as 'journal: <key> chain broken'. Reproduced twice: todo:78 at 2026-10-04T06:36:30 (two nodes, same ts, both prev=a6771ba6641a) and todo:91 at 2026-10-08T09:15:59 (two nodes, same ts, both prev=fd7c251ca64c). Mechanism: kanban_slot_chain apply/app_planner.slot_chain appends journal nodes without cross-process locking; the store's _atomic_write makes each FILE write atomic but two sessions applying within the same window each compute a parent from their own read snapshot. The journal is append-only (never rewritten, per policy — both breaks left in place), so verify stays red until fixed. Fix direction: lock or compare-and-swap on (slot_key, parent) at append time — reread the tail immediately before write and rebase the node if the tip moved. Evidence: .kanban/slot_history.jsonl chains todo:78, todo:91.

[DONE 2026-10-10] Landed 8ca177458 on fix/journal-append-race.
Root cause: apply_board derived every node's parent from an UNLOCKED tail
snapshot; the flock inside append_lines only serializes bytes, not the
read->derive->append decision, so overlapping writers forked the chain.
Measured on the live journal: 788 breaks, not the 2 this card cites, plus a
second mode the card missed (an identical node appended twice, duplicate
slot_prev for one card_id).
Fix: append_lines_checked(lines, expected_size, rebase) - size check and
write share one flock; unchanged size writes the snapshot (cost: one fstat,
so nothing is serialized onto the ~1s board-write path), moved size runs
rebase() with the lock held. expected_size is captured BEFORE the read:
a stat taken after would agree with an already-stale read and mask the
contention. apply_board split into plan (tail-independent) / derive (pure
over tips) so rebase redoes only the tail-dependent half.
Proof: tests/test_slot_chain_concurrency.py - a barrier releases 4 procs
together and each stalls inside the vulnerable window; against UNFIXED
sources it fails with 9 chain forks (3 slots x 3 losing writers),
reproducing todo:78/todo:91 deterministically. Passes with the fix.
Gates: 200 passed (app-planner) + 3 passed test_store_write_guard, ruff
check+format clean. Live board on a copy: verify 788 -> 788 (delta 0),
journal byte delta 0 on re-apply, move_card 0.90/0.79/1.32s vs
1.19/0.91/1.01s baseline.
OPEN: the 788 historical forks are NOT repaired - append-only policy
forbids rewriting them, and this card leaves them in place, so verify
stays red until that is decided.
COORDINATION: fix/slot-chain-append-race existed as a name-only stub
pointing at main with zero work; not used, as checking it out would
clobber the live board+journals. 89d464266 (board.jsonl OCC) is separate
and still stranded on 8+ branches; it never touched slot_chain.py.
title: slot_history.jsonl append race — concurrent apply leaves stale-parent nodes (todo:78, todo:91 breaks)

description:
## Symptom

8 router test files collect-fail with `ImportError: cannot import name 'build_test_app' from 'conftest' (/home/mana/Documents/Default Project/sloughGPT/conftest.py)` — but ONLY when pytest is invoked with an explicit file list. A bare run or a directory argument collects all 8 and they pass.

Affected (all `tests/core-py/`): test_health_router, test_inference_router, test_kb_router, test_mobile_router, test_models_router, test_self_train_router, test_souls_router, test_system_router.

## Root cause (systematic)

`from conftest import build_test_app` is resolved through `sys.path`, and which `conftest.py` wins depends on what lands at `sys.path[0]`:

- `sys.path[0] = packages/core-py` (relative, from `pythonpath` in pytest.ini) -> `packages/core-py/conftest.py`, the SHIM that does `from tests.conftest import build_test_app` -> OK
- `sys.path[0] = <repo root>` (absolute, after root `conftest.py` runs its `sys.path.insert(0, repo_root)` / remove+insert block) -> root `conftest.py`, which has 0 hits for `build_test_app` -> ImportError

Reproduced with a debug plugin printing `sys.modules["conftest"].__file__` and `sys.path[:5]` at `pytest_collection_finish`:

- `pytest tests/` (directory arg) -> `conftest` = `packages/core-py/conftest.py` (shim) -> 0 errors
- `pytest tests/core-py/test_health_router.py` (file arg) -> `conftest` = root `conftest.py` -> ImportError
- `pytest tests/core-py/test_a*.py ... test_n*.py` (expanded glob = file list) -> same ImportError

So the deciding factor is the invocation shape, not the code. It is a latent landmine: any chunked/scoped run that passes files explicitly will report phantom collection errors that a canonical run does not.

Confirmed NOT a consolidation regression: at `dcb2a5eaf^` (pre-move) `build_test_app` was likewise absent from root `conftest.py`, `--import-mode=importlib` already existed, and the shim already existed. A bare full-tree collect at 04:18 (`final_collect.txt`) showed 0 such errors.

## Evidence

- 8 phantom events across the chunked run: C2_en=5, C3b2_left=1, C3d_rest_s=2
- Re-run through a directory arg + `-k` (`H_eight_files.txt`): **115 passed, 0 failed** -> the files themselves are green
- shim: `packages/core-py/conftest.py` = `from tests.conftest import build_test_app`
- root: `conftest.py` has no `build_test_app`

## Proposed fix (needs approval)

Make the import deterministic instead of `sys.path`-order dependent. Options, cheapest first:

1. Root `conftest.py` re-exports `build_test_app` (one line: `from tests.conftest import build_test_app  # noqa: F401`) so both winning resolutions succeed.
2. Or change the 8 test files to import from `tests.conftest` directly (package-qualified, immune to `sys.path[0]`).

Option 1 is the smallest blast radius and also un-breaks any other explicit-file invocation.

## Impact on accounting

These 8 events were subtracted from the full-suite totals as invocation artifacts (777 raw -> 769 real).
DUPLICATE of ccec0b63 (append race d708578d — identical description, title lost its quoted string). Closing; canonical card = ccec0b63.
CLOSED as duplicate of ccec0b63.
title: PHANTOM collection errors: explicit file-list args flip sys.path[0] so  resolves to root conftest (8 router files; bare/dir run collects them, 115 pass)

## Root cause (systematic)

`from conftest import build_test_app` is resolved through `sys.path`, and which `conftest.py` wins depends on what lands at `sys.path[0]`:

- `sys.path[0] = packages/core-py` (relative, from `pythonpath` in pytest.ini) -> `packages/core-py/conftest.py`, the SHIM that does `from tests.conftest import build_test_app` -> OK
- `sys.path[0] = <repo root>` (absolute, after root `conftest.py` runs its `sys.path.insert(0, repo_root)` / remove+insert block) -> root `conftest.py`, which has 0 hits for `build_test_app` -> ImportError

Reproduced with a debug plugin printing `sys.modules["conftest"].__file__` and `sys.path[:5]` at `pytest_collection_finish`:

- `pytest tests/` (directory arg) -> `conftest` = `packages/core-py/conftest.py` (shim) -> 0 errors
- `pytest tests/core-py/test_health_router.py` (file arg) -> `conftest` = root `conftest.py` -> ImportError
- `pytest tests/core-py/test_a*.py ... test_n*.py` (expanded glob = file list) -> same ImportError

So the deciding factor is the invocation shape, not the code. It is a latent landmine: any chunked/scoped run that passes files explicitly will report phantom collection errors that a canonical run does not.

Confirmed NOT a consolidation regression: at `dcb2a5eaf^` (pre-move) `build_test_app` was likewise absent from root `conftest.py`, `--import-mode=importlib` already existed, and the shim already existed. A bare full-tree collect at 04:18 (`final_collect.txt`) showed 0 such errors.

## Evidence

- 8 phantom events across the chunked run: C2_en=5, C3b2_left=1, C3d_rest_s=2
- Re-run through a directory arg + `-k` (`H_eight_files.txt`): **115 passed, 0 failed** -> the files themselves are green
- shim: `packages/core-py/conftest.py` = `from tests.conftest import build_test_app`
- root: `conftest.py` has no `build_test_app`

## Proposed fix (needs approval)

Make the import deterministic instead of `sys.path`-order dependent. Options, cheapest first:

1. Root `conftest.py` re-exports `build_test_app` (one line: `from tests.conftest import build_test_app  # noqa: F401`) so both winning resolutions succeed.
2. Or change the 8 test files to import from `tests.conftest` directly (package-qualified, immune to `sys.path[0]`).

Option 1 is the smallest blast radius and also un-breaks any other explicit-file invocation.

## Impact on accounting

These 8 events were subtracted from the full-suite totals as invocation artifacts (777 raw -> 769 real).
PICKED UP (2026-10-08, user-approved): fix chosen = change the 8 test files to `from tests.conftest import build_test_app` (package-qualified, canonical home, immune to sys.path[0] order; root conftest.py untouched). Rationale: packages/core-py/tests/ no longer exists so tests.conftest has exactly ONE resolution (root tests/conftest.py). Red reproduced in worktree first (file-arg run -> 1 collection error), green in both invocation shapes after. NOTE: bb04fa4a is a duplicate of this card (append race d708578d).
SHIPPED 2026-10-09 commit 512566301 on fix/phantom-conftest-import (base 3359f412b, worktree .wt-phantom), pushed to origin. Fix = the 8 test files now do 'from tests.conftest import build_test_app' (user-approved option). RED first: explicit file-list probe -> 3 collection errors. GREEN after: explicit 8-file list 115 passed / 0 failed (matches the card's canonical dir evidence), dir-arg + -k 115 passed / 0 failed, ruff clean. Shared synced 8/8 byte-identical + re-verified 115 passed in shared. OBSERVED (not fixed, shell/TUI lane): tests/core-py/test_shell_tui_live.py collection-errors in directory runs at BASE too (stash comparison) — its module domain.shell._internal.term_screen is not in the tree. INSIGHT: full tests/core-py/ dir run exceeds 10 min — chunked file-list runs are the norm, which is exactly why this phantom mattered. Duplicate card bb04fa4a closed.

[VERIFIED 2026-10-13 foreman] CLOSED — landing 549b3e58a (10-09, 'fix(tests): package-qualify build_test_app imports — kills phantom collection errors on explicit file lists (card ccec0b63)') is ancestor of BOTH integration-sync and the local lane (91605e1d4 / 512566301 are the stranded sibling copies of the same fix on other branches — port-class, not rework). Gates re-run on integration-sync @fa9ee4e8b: explicit file-list of ALL 11 current importers (the card's 8 core-py router tests + 3 later additions: test_api_keys, test_inference_generate, test_meta_weight_merge) = 152 passed / 0 collection errors in 8s; the card's canonical 8-file list collects exactly 115 tests — byte-matches the card's '115 passed' evidence. The card's side-observation is also RESOLVED on this line: domain/shell/_internal/term_screen.py is present (TUI port 23776c16a) and tests/core-py/test_shell_tui_live.py now collects 42 tests cleanly (it collection-errored at their base). description:
PROBLEM — 12 chat-test failures share one root cause: a production connectivity gate the tests never stub.

Scope: tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py, chunk C3g (81 failures total).
Signature split of C3g's 81: 28 `_interpret_natural` missing · 21 other assertion ·
15 init-None shutdown · **12 API-connectivity gated** · 2 event_bus · 2 ImportError · 1 other.
The 12 are one coherent bucket and had not been separated out before.

The 12:
  TestCmdChat::test_chat_no_args, ::test_chat_reset
  TestCmdChatExtra::test_chat_no_args, ::test_chat_reset, ::test_chat_success
  TestCmdChatExecution::test_chat_no_args, ::test_chat_reset, ::test_chat_new_session, ::test_chat_continues_session
  TestCmdChatDeeper::test_chat_no_args
  TestCmdChatDeeperV5::test_no_args, ::test_reset_session

ROOT CAUSE
`ShellREPL._require_api` (domain/shell/_internal/repl.py:4245) reads `self.os.api_status`;
when unavailable it prints "✗ API server is not connected. Use 'api start' to launch it.",
sets `self._last_exit_code = 1`, returns False. `_cmd_chat` consults it.

Three distinct failure modes:
  (a) test_chat_no_args — NO stub at all. Real gate runs -> exit code 1.
      Assert: `assert repl._last_exit_code == 0` -> `assert 1 == 0`.
  (b) test_chat_reset — gate fires before the local `/reset` mutation, so
      `_chat_session_id` stays "old". Assert: `assert 'old' is None`.
      FAILS ON STATE, not exit code. Relaxing the exit assert does NOT fix this.
  (c) test_chat_success — patches `_require_api` AND `_spinner_call`, but the send path
      has a SECOND connectivity check emitting "Error: Cannot connect to API server",
      so the patched `_spinner_call` is never reached. `_chat_history` stays length 1.

Contrast — two variants in the SAME run pass and prove both points:
  * TestCmdChatDeeperV2::test_chat_no_args PASSES because it uses the tolerant form:
        out = _run_with_io(repl, [], lambda: repl._cmd_chat(""))
        assert "Usage" in out or repl._last_exit_code == 1
  * test_chat_no_api PASSES because it patches `_require_api` directly.

CAUSAL TIMELINE (git archaeology)
  2026-07-30  e19f96190  chat tests first land (at the pre-move path)
  2026-09-13  68c427af5  "feat: add startup optimization suggestions" — 197 files,
                         +105,486 lines. Creates domain/shell/_internal/repl.py
                         (4,652 lines, all inserted) INCLUDING `_require_api`.
    git show 68c427af5^:.../repl.py | grep -c 'def _require_api'  ->  0
    git show 68c427af5:.../repl.py   | grep -c 'def _require_api'  ->  1
    That commit's --stat does NOT list test_shell_repl_more.py.
  => The gate arrived ~6 weeks AFTER the tests, and that commit did not adapt them.
     Not original test debt; introduced 2026-09-13.

NOT ANOTHER SESSION'S WIP
  git diff domain/shell/_internal/repl.py  ->  1 line, a comment typo
  (line ~330: "domains.logging" -> "domain.logging"). Nothing near
  `_require_api` (4245) or `_cmd_chat` (3317). Failures are against committed HEAD.

NO BASELINE AVAILABLE
  ~/.cache/sloughgpt-gate1/failures.txt (pre-move baseline, 2026-10-06 05:42)
  contains 0 entries for test_shell_repl_more. run6's testpaths never included it
  (gap math in ~/.cache/sloughgpt-gate1/FULL_SUITE_REPORT.md). So NEW-vs-pre-existing
  cannot be settled from run6 data — the git timeline above is the evidence instead.
  NOTE: a direct run at 68c427af5^ was NOT executed (shared worktree, branch must not
  be switched), so before/after execution is unproven; the timeline is inferential.

FIX OPTIONS
  1. PRODUCTION (recommended for a + b) — exempt local operations from the gate.
     Empty-args usage/help and `/reset` mutate only local state and should not require
     a live API. Printing "API server is not connected" instead of Usage for an empty
     argument is arguably a UX defect on its own.
  2. TEST (required for c) — stub the second connectivity check on the send path so
     the already-patched `_spinner_call` is actually reached.
  3. REJECTED — relax assertions to the TestCmdChatDeeperV2 style. Cannot fix (b),
     which fails on state (`_chat_session_id` still "old"), and it would mask whether
     `/reset` worked at all.

DECISION NEEDED
  Is (b) a product question? Should `/reset` clear local chat session state while
  disconnected? Recommended: yes, it is local state. Option 1 then fixes a + b
  behaviorally and option 2 covers c.

EVIDENCE
  ~/.cache/sloughgpt-gate1/suite/C3g_shell_repl_more.txt
    lines 1540-1543  FAILED markers
    lines 4217-4250  the three tracebacks with captured stdout
title: chat tests fail on production API-connectivity gate added 2026-09-13

description:
GOAL — make the code speak the operator vocabulary agreed with the user.

AGREED VOCABULARY (user's words, verified against CSS cascade):
  mode    = the sun/moon light-dark switch      -> code 'mode' / man_mode (unchanged)
  theme   = the color switch (the widget)       -> useTheme() itself
  color   = the 7-chip highlighter that recolors --primary/--ring ONLY (buttons, rings)
            code calls this 'theme' / man_theme  -> rename to color / man_color
  palette = Noir Violet, Neural Precision — full-spectrum VSCode-theme-like scheme
            code already calls it palette / man_palette (unchanged)

WHY SOUND — apps/web/app/globals.css @tokens:auras (generated, carries the invariant):
auras override ONLY --primary/--ring; palettes own background/card/secondary/muted/
border/charts/shadows. Palette x aura cascade bug: an aura must never set surface
tokens. The user's mental model IS the mechanism.

MUST NOT BE CALLED 'accent' — --accent is an unrelated token (warm peach 236 145 95
in noir-violet, sky 56 189 248 in neural-precision) used by badges + chart-3.
Two meanings of accent is the exact confusion being removed.

SCOPE
  rename: lib/theme-storage.ts -> lib/appearance.ts; context -> { mode, color, palette };
          ThemeSwitcher labels/aria; sync-html-theme; settings/page.tsx:81;
          5 test files asserting theme-purple / man_theme; docs DESIGN_SYSTEM.md:129
          + .opencode/skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md:26.
  generator: packages/strui/scripts/gen-tokens.mjs:114-115 emits html.theme-<id> ->
          html.color-<id>; regen BOTH globals.css marker regions + doc table; gate --check.
  migration: man_theme -> man_color with read-fallback (read new, else old, write new,
          delete old) or every user's saved look resets to purple. Ids (purple,
          noir-violet) are persisted data and do NOT change.

BUG FIXED IN SAME CHANGE — apps/web/index.html:24-26 bootstrap reads unprefixed
  localStorage 'theme'/'mode'/'palette' while the app writes man_theme/man_mode/
  man_palette. Nothing writes the unprefixed keys, so the pre-paint bootstrap ALWAYS
  misses: every load paints dark theme-purple then flips to the real choice (flash).
  Its id lists are also stale: palettes [ocean,sunrise,forest,monochrome] (real set is
  noir-violet, neural-precision), theme list contains a nonexistent 'yellow', and it
  hardcodes mode=dark while getInitialMode() honours prefers-color-scheme.
  Comment at line 18 claims 'synced with theme-storage' — it drifted.

OUT OF SCOPE — palette.json values, apps/mobile/src/theme/palette.generated.ts,
  the --accent token, mode semantics, and the primary-only aura invariant.

ACCEPTANCE — index updated (no new app/package/doc: rename only, docs updated in
  place), shared copy reused (root node_modules only, no new lockfile), coordination
  named (target files were clean of other sessions' WIP at branch time; HEAD was
  feat/vm-asm-intake with ~60 dirty files belonging to other sessions — none of them
  theme files).

GATES — eslint, tsc, vitest (5 theme test files), node packages/strui/scripts/gen-tokens.mjs --check

description:
REPORTED: clicking Load on Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct raised the global banner 'Lazy load requested for ... but ProcessGuard could not be started' (logs/sloughgpt.log 11:11:34-11:11:59, rid=b21f462a).

ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed, reproduced 1:1 outside the server):
1. The guard worker child posts ('dead', pid) on hb_q and ('error', None, 'Model load failed: ...') on resp_q, then returns from _slo_worker_main -> the child process exits at ~25s.
2. ModelWorkerProcess.start() sees the death and breaks out of the ready-wait loop immediately (25s, not 300s), but ALWAYS formats the failure as 'Worker[...]: failed to start within 300.0s' - a constant, not elapsed time.
3. The worker's own error payload on resp_q is never drained during startup, so the true cause ('NoneType' object has no attribute 'matmul_int8_select_kernel') never reaches the operator. Only the log has it.
4. _build_process_guard() returns None -> _load_hf_model raises -> controllers/models.py:181 raises the banner message.

BUILD:
- model_worker.ModelWorkerProcess.start(): distinguish exited / reported-dead / timed-out, report elapsed seconds and the child exitcode, and drain the resp_q error payload into the exception text.
- Regression test: a real worker child pointed at a missing .slnc must fail fast with the worker's own message, not a fake timeout.

COORDINATION (card 8e46f3e7 'Remove packages/core-py/domains' - that port is in flight in the shared tree): the wrapper port moved domain/infrastructure/_internal/quant_core/wrapper.py out of the core-py alias but did NOT carry matmul_int8.c / matmul_int4.c, which still live only in packages/core-py/domains/infrastructure/quant_core/. Until they travel with the implementation, _build_all finds no source, no .so is built, and quantized matmul silently runs the numpy fallback (~12.6x slower - card 200). The _LIB=None import crash from the same gap was patched in the working tree at 06:06 today (not by this session).

Card: aab5df8b-6e04-47b3-966b-43563f7c5f44
Commit: b2ba18527 (feat/caret-core)

## Problem

12 chat-test failures shared one root cause: `_require_api("chat")` sat
*before dispatch* in `_cmd_chat` (repl.py:3337), so a network precondition
gated subcommands that never touch the network. `/reset` and `/status` mutate
or read local session state only; bare `chat` enters a prompt loop.

## Fix (2 parts, both production)

1. Move the gate from the command entry into `_chat_send` — the only site
   doing HTTP, reached by both the direct path and `_cmd_chat_interactive`.
   Placed *before* the history append so the send path's output, history and
   exit code stay bit-for-bit unchanged.
2. Guard the empty-arg branch on `self.io.owns_stdin` (the declaration-not-
   probe seam `/logs -f` already uses at repl.py:2717): False -> print Usage,
   exit 0; True -> interactive mode as documented.

Part 2 was forced by measurement, not preference. `_cmd_chat_interactive`
reads with builtin `input()`, which raises `OSError: pytest: reading from
stdin while output is captured!` under capture, and the loop only catches
EOFError/KeyboardInterrupt. A gate-only change converted 5 assertion failures
into 5 errors and added 1 NEW failure (TestCmdChatDeeperV2 passed at baseline
on its `or exit == 1` disjunct).

## Behaviour deltas

- `chat /reset`  API down -> `[session cleared]`, exit 0 (was warning, exit 1)
- `chat /status` API down -> session info, exit 0 (was warning, exit 1)
- bare `chat`, no terminal -> Usage, exit 0 (was warning, exit 1)
- bare `chat`, real terminal -> unchanged (interactive)
- bare `chat`, TUI -> Usage (was raw input() across the curses screen)
- `chat <msg>` API down -> UNCHANGED: same warning, exit 1, history intact
- interactive mode: 278us per 20 messages of gating (was 14us/session)
- other 10 `_require_api` sites and `_cmd_ai` untouched

## Tests

3 approved one-line `repl.cmds = MagicMock()` stubs (test_chat_success,
test_chat_new_session, test_chat_continues_session) — those tests stubbed the
stale `_spinner_call`/`cmds.chat` collaborator while production streams via
`cmds.chat_stream`, so history came up short (`assert 1 == 2`). Pattern matches
the already-passing sibling `test_chat_with_response`; 33 existing uses in the
file. No assertion weakened.

## Verification

- red first: `12 failed in 3.37s`, all assertions for the right reason
- test_shell_repl_more.py: 81 -> 69 failed, 4025 -> 4037 passed
  set-diff vs recorded 81-id baseline: FIXED 12, **NEW 0**
- the 12 + DeeperV2: 13/13 passed
- test_repl_execute.py + test_api_provider.py: 51 passed (other _cmd_chat callers)
- scripts/benchmark_chat_dispatch.py (new) 3/3 rc=0 — exact probe counts:
  reset 0, status 0, usage 0, gate_down 1; gate 13.9us vs 2ms ceiling;
  probe is in-memory at 8.8us
- ruff + py_compile clean on all three files
title: chat API gate moved to the sink: /reset, /status and bare chat work offline (aab5df8b)

description:
FOUND WHILE: cleanup-agent sweep 2026-10-09, root-causing a suite timeout.

SYMPTOM: tests/api-server/test_knowledge_router.py::test_stats_with_many_facts_terminates times out (120s). It POSTs 250 facts; each POST /knowledge costs ~1.3-1.8s -> ~325s total.

ROOT CAUSE (two compounding defects, both verified by cProfile):
(1) O(N) full index rebuild per single-document insert. ProductionRAG.add_document (domain/cognition/_internal/rag.py:616) chunks the doc, add_chunk()s each, then calls retriever.build_index() -> BM25Indexer.index(self.chunks) (rag.py:69), which re-tokenizes and rebuilds inverted_index/doc_freq/doc_lengths from scratch over ALL chunks. Measured: 42,759 _tokenize calls from rag.py:69 for ONE insert.
(2) The chunk list is unbounded for the life of the process. HybridRetriever.add_chunk (rag.py:193) only appends; there is no self.chunks = [] / .clear() anywhere in rag.py, and get_rag_service() is a process-lifetime singleton (rag_service.py:660) with no reset API. So chunks accumulate monotonically; the KB store cleanup clears entries.json but NOT the retriever chunk list, so the index keeps growing across tests and across a long-lived server.

The API already documents this trap: add_document(rebuild_index=False) + build_index() once at the end. rag_service uses that for bulk paths (rag_service.py:105,136,411) but the single-insert endpoint path uses the default rebuild_index=True.

IMPACT: unbounded memory growth + insert latency that grows linearly with corpus size, in a production server process.

PROPOSED FIX (needs approval, not applied — core algorithmic change in another lane's active worktree):
(a) Make indexing incremental: on add_chunk, append postings and update doc_freq/doc_lengths/num_docs incrementally instead of rebuilding. BM25Indexer.index() keeps its reset-and-rebuild path for the explicit bulk build_index() call.
(b) Add a bounded-growth guard / reset API on the retriever (e.g. retriever.clear()) and call it from the knowledge-store cleanup path so tests and purges actually reset the index.
(c) Have the single-document endpoint path batch: add with rebuild_index=False, then build once.

VERIFICATION AVAILABLE: rerun tests/api-server/test_knowledge_router.py::test_stats_with_many_facts_terminates with --timeout; expect 250 inserts well under timeout. Also benchmark scripts/benchmark_slonet.py is unrelated; a dedicated micro-bench of inserts/sec vs corpus size is the right measurement.

COORDINATION: repo worktree was concurrently mutated during this session (branch switched 06:10:32/06:10:43; commits 3d49ff923 and 465eecc8b landed mid-session). Carded rather than patched for that reason.
title: RAG: per-insert full BM25 rebuild over an unbounded singleton chunk list — latency grows without bound
