description:
Compat matrix finding (docs/VM_COMPAT.md, bweeper row): after the intake cards landed, bweeper.asm assembles (562 bytes), spawn honors its `org 0x7c00` (EIP=0x7C00), and it RUNS — then faults at step 4: MemFault: read8 out of bounds at 0x660821EA. Root cause: X86CPU decodes with a 32-bit default operand size only; real-mode ([BITS 16]) sources emit un-prefixed 16-bit encodings, so `b8 03 00 cd 10` (mov ax,3 / int 0x10) decodes as `mov eax, 0x10CD0003` and swallows the following instruction's bytes. Fault-state evidence: eax=0x10CD0203, ebx=0x21BA0000 (int 10h / mov-dx immediates consumed), EIP=0x7C14. All 5 corpus programs are [BITS 16] → this is the next tier-2 wall behind the intake gates: any BITS 16 program that assembles is then garbage-executed. Fix direction (design review first — large CPU change): CPU mode state (default operand size 16 + default address size 16 + real-mode segment bases, latched from the assembler's final bits/org at spawn), or an explicit 16→32 translation pass at load. Related: BIOS INT tier card 508245c0 depends on this — INT 10h services must dispatch under real-mode conventions. Evidence: scripts/compat/matrix.json bweeper fault row; repro = spawn bweeper.asm + step 4.

APPROACH (2026-10-09, recon probes): NO CPU mode-state redesign. Four independent defects, each fixed smaller:
(1) operand-size inversion — `_pfx` emits 0x66 when operand size != BITS mode (real-hw faithful) but the CPU
reads 0x66 as always-16-bit-op; the two agree only in BITS 32. Fix: unify `_pfx`/`_pfx_size` on "emit 0x66 iff
the op is 16-bit ON OUR CPU"; BITS 32 emission stays byte-identical (REG16 in 32 stays True, REG32 in 16
flips True->False), BITS 16 r16 ops gain the prefix `_exec_16bit` already executes (b8-bf, ALU, modrm, lea,
inc, push, string — probe-confirmed). The mem<->reg16 and word/dword-imm mov sites ALREADY use this exact
convention (vm.py:4814 comment) — unification makes _pfx agree with the codebase's own documented rule.
(2) silent address loss — 16-bit base regs ([si]/[di]/[bx]/[bp] and combos) are not in _REG32, so
_mem_operand resolves them to [disp32=0] and drops displacements ([bx+0x50e] -> [0x0], probe-confirmed).
Fix: flat mapping si->esi, di->edi, bx->ebx, bp->ebp (+SIB for bx+si/bx+di/bp+si/bp+di), incl. the
[ebp] mod0-rm5-without-disp decode trap (force disp8=0).
(3) `es:[..]` assembles to ZERO bytes (operand starting with 'seg:' matches no _emit_mov branch) and the
CPU has no segment-prefix handling. Fix: emit the NASM-faithful prefix byte (26/2E/36/3E/64/65) at dispatch,
CPU skips segment prefixes (flat model: segments are no-ops).
(4) 66 e8/e9/c3 unknown in `_exec_16bit` (probe: InsFault) — BITS 16 emits bare e8 rel16 (4679) which the
main path reads as rel32 -> desync. Fix: bits16 near call/jmp emit 0x66 + rel16 (rel base +4), and
_exec_16bit gains e8 (push return EIP32 + rel16 target), e9 (rel16), c3 (pop EIP32) — flat-consistent stack.
Deliberately NOT in scope (documented, not blocking bweeper): 66 FF/66 C1 handlers, loop's ECX-vs-CX (safe
while high halves are zero), far jmp offsets, real-mode IP16 truncation, BIOS int service semantics (separate
BIOS card). Unknown int vectors already return silently (probe), so BIOS-tier corpus programs can run.

SHIPPED (2026-10-09, branch feat/vm-bits16-flat): all four fixes landed —
_pfx/_pfx_size unified (r16 always 66, r32/dword never; r32 acc imm always
imm32 — the bits16 imm16 shortening desynced once prefixes were gone);
16-bit base regs flat-map ([si]->[esi] etc, [ebp]/SIB-ebp mod00 -> mod01
disp8=0); segment qualifiers emit 26/2E/36/3E/64/65 and CPU skips them;
bits16 near call/jmp emit 66 E8/E9 rel16 + _exec_16bit e8/e9/c3 handlers.
_estimator sizes updated (push/pop r16=2, word strings=2, rep word=3,
jmp/call bits16=4). VERDICT: bweeper asm_gap -> budget (assembles, runs the
full 300k step budget, no fault). Evidence: emission 180 green (10 new
TestBits16VMEmission + 96 inverted-convention pins updated), compat_track
green incl. new test_probe_bweeper_runs_to_budget, os_layer 1321 passed /
7 failed (all 7 fail at baseline 4a5132698), vm zone = baseline 19,
cave benchmark hud_ok=true (2241.8 ms/frame mean), matrix.json only-row
change = bweeper. Out-of-scope items confirmed latent (documented above).
title: X86CPU lacks 16-bit default operand size (real mode) — every [BITS 16] program misparses bytes

description:
Commit: 740ea0b26 (feat/caret-core)
Scope: second bucket of the test_shell_repl_more.py tail — 15 failures, one
root cause. (Previous: 65ca94433, the 28 `_interpret_natural` skips.)

## Root cause

`domain/shell/_internal/runtime.py:383` — `DaitRuntime.shutdown()`
dereferenced `self._init`, which is `None` from `__init__` (322) until
`boot()` populates it (343):

    AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'shutdown'
    15 of 15 failures, zero other reasons

    TestCmdShutdown* 6, TestCmdExit*+ExportStateExitHistory 6,
    TestCmdBootShutdown* 3

The codebase already treats "not booted yet" as real in two places —
`status_summary` (423: `if self._boot_complete and self._init is not None`)
and `_cmd_svc` (4321: "Init system not booted yet. Run 'boot' first."). This
was the one path that forgot.

Latent rather than active: production calls `os.boot()` at repl.py:5207 before
the prompt. Still a crash on a user command, and all 15 assert the correct
contract (exit 0, `_running -> False`).

## Shipped in two iterations — first guard was wrong

Attempt 1 (ternary on the dereference) cleared the 15 but added a NEW
failure: it left `kernel.shutdown()` + `reset_device_system()` running on the
never-booted path, and both are module-level singletons, so they tore down
state this runtime never created and leaked that to every later test.
Full-file runs went 41 -> 27/29 with whoami NEW, 3 runs running.

Attempt 2 (shipped) returns before touching anything:

    if self._init is None:
        return ""

`boot()` is what creates the devices (344) and boots the kernel (354), so an
unbooted runtime has nothing to tear down. This also matches what the
crashing code did — it stopped dead, so nothing after it ran. The comment
records the leak, because the obvious defensive fix is the one that breaks.

## Verification

    pre-change 41 -> 26 failed;  4052 passed;  36 skipped; total 4114
    NEW vs pre-change: 0      cleared: 15
    5 consecutive clean full-file runs: 26/4052/36 (177s, 140s, 94s, 75s, 434s)
    ruff + py_compile clean;  15 target tests + whoami = 16 passed

## Flakes investigated, not hand-waved

3 of 8 full runs also reported `test_whoami_via_execute` and 2 `du` tests.
Not this change: neither `whoami` nor `du` has a Python handler, so both go
through `_execute_single`'s system-binary `subprocess.run` fallback where
`except Exception` -> exit 1; `uptime` (which has a handler) never flakes.
Isolated they pass 25/25 at load average 25.9 where the guard never runs. All
3 flake runs took 434-534s under concurrent load; every run since is 26-clean
with NEW=0.

No benchmark covers this path (none of scripts/benchmark_*.py exercise
shutdown; not a training/inference change).

## Remaining

26 failures left in the file: 10 `assert X in X` substring asserts,
3 `domain.infrastructure` missing-attribute (config/event_bus), 2 mock
ImportError, plus assorted singles.

__init__.py still re-exports the symbols (get_config, get_event_bus, EventBus)

description:
FOUND WHILE: measuring the RAG per-insert fix (card 4563be94). That fix landed and took POST /knowledge from ~1300-1800ms to 45-81ms, but test_stats_with_many_facts_terminates STILL times out — so a second O(N^2) remains, here in persistence.

DEFECT (domain/memory/_internal/knowledge_store.py): _save_entries() (L684) and _save_visited() (L664) do a full-table rewrite on EVERY single add:
  1. self._entries_col.drop()          <- drops the whole collection
  2. self._entries_col.insert_many(data) <- re-inserts EVERY entry
  3. ENTRIES_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(data))  <- rewrites the whole JSON
and _save_visited() does the identical drop + insert_many(all) + JSON rewrite for visited hashes.

So one insert costs O(corpus) writes, three times over -> O(N^2) to ingest N facts. Measured: 250 inserts = >119s (pytest timeout), 100 inserts = 148s in a direct harness, with very erratic per-insert times (3513ms, 492ms, 3274ms, 1714ms, 1404ms).

AMPLIFIER: the run logs 'mogdb open errors: replayed=4828 quarantined=0'. The crash-resistant journal added in 06:06:22 fsyncs appends, so re-inserting the whole corpus multiplies that cost.

SECOND DEFECT (same file, worse): _save_entries() drops the collection BEFORE re-inserting. A crash or exception between the drop and the insert loses the entire vector store. This is a data-loss hazard, not just a performance one.

PROPOSED FIX (needs approval — persistence semantics + data-loss risk, and MogDB is another lane's active work right now):
(a) Replace drop+reinsert-all with targeted upserts: one upsert per added entry, one delete per removed entry. Keep a full-rewrite path only for explicit compaction/repair.
(b) Stop mirroring the full corpus into legacy JSON on every add — write it on shutdown or on a debounced interval, not per request.
(c) Same treatment for _save_visited(): append hashes incrementally instead of dropping and re-inserting the set.
(d) Make the save crash-safe: write to a temp path and atomically rename, so a crash can never leave the store empty.

MEASUREMENT: rerun tests/api-server/test_knowledge_router.py::test_stats_with_many_facts_terminates --timeout=110; expect it to pass. Micro-bench inserts/sec vs corpus size before and after.

NOT APPLIED: deliberately left alone. MogDB/journal work is in flight in this shared worktree (another session committed 3d49ff923 and e6a8cf601 today) and this touches write/durability semantics — too risky to change unilaterally.
title: knowledge_store: every single add drops+rewrites ALL entries and visited hashes (second O(N^2), persistence layer)

description:
Correction to commit 740ea0b26 ("fix(shell): make shutdown() tolerate a
runtime that never booted"), section "The two flakes, investigated rather
than hand-waved".

The commit message states:

    Neither `whoami` nor `du` has a Python handler, so both route through
    `_execute_single`'s system-binary `subprocess.run` fallback, where
    `except Exception` maps any spawn/timeout pressure to exit code 1.

**That is true for `du` and FALSE for `whoami`.** Found while tracing the
command registry for 47df0ffce.

## Actual mechanism for whoami

`whoami` is an alias of the `souls_cmd` extension module:

    domain/shell/cmds/__init__.py:87
        "souls_cmd": ["souls", "switch", "whoami"],

`_execute_single` resolves it to `ext_mod`, so it never reaches the
`shutil.which()` binary fallback:

    if handler is None and ext_mod is None:   # <- binary fallback
    ...
    if ext_mod:
        self._last_exit_code = ext_mod.run(argv, c, self.cmds, self._env)

and the ext path wraps `run()` in its own `except Exception` ->
`_format_error` -> `_last_exit_code = 1`. So a whoami failure is
`souls_cmd.run()` raising, not a subprocess spawn/timeout.

`du` genuinely has neither handler nor ext module, so it does take the
binary path. The two tests therefore fail for **different** reasons and do
not share a mechanism — my message implied they did.

## What still holds

- Load-window correlation: every failing run took 434-534s; every run since
  (75-240s) is clean.
- Isolation: 25/25 pass at load average 25.9, where the shutdown guard is
  never executed.
- The shipped guard itself: 5 of 6 runs clean, and all recent runs show
  NEW=0 vs the pre-change baseline.

## What does not hold

The shared-mechanism claim. Also note the first two of those three failing
runs were with the *superseded* attempt-1 guard (the ternary that ran
`kernel.shutdown()` + `reset_device_system()` on an unbooted runtime); the
shipped early-return guard does not execute those calls at all. So those two
failures were caused by my first attempt, not by external load — which the
commit message's "they are not this change" framing understates for that
attempt (it is correct for the shipped one).

No code change: `740ea0b26` behaves as described and verified. This is a
prose correction only, recorded here rather than by rewriting history —
rewording 740ea0b26 would re-SHA it and 0a5a048b7, and would invalidate the
reference in note ba7a3546.
title: [CORRECTION] 740ea0b26 whoami flake mechanism wrong — whoami dispatches via souls_cmd ext, not the binary fallback

description: Root cause (probes A-E, 2026-10-09): SloughGPTTrainer.train() parks the cyclic GC (_gc_parked, perf: 2.9 vs 31 steps/s) and _gc_parked_step collects only every _GC_COLLECT_EVERY_STEPS=50 steps. Measured per-step cyclic garbage = ~769MB (probe A: RSS 75->1191->1960->2728->3496MB, linear); first collection at step 50, but OOM death at step 8-12 on the 23GB box => zero collections before death. Probe B proved collectible (per-step gc.collect => flat 1170MB); probe E captured edges (closure cells, lists, Tensor.grad). One-time ~1.1GB at step1 = numba JIT (not a leak). API jobs die at step ~12 (see card bde58796). Fix plan (TDD): RSS-triggered collection in _gc_parked_step (SLO_TRAIN_GC_MB, default 512MB growth since last collect) + keep 50-step cadence as fallback; integration test asserts bounded pending garbage. Related done: 20260812 _consumers leak (b7007f4).

description:
Finding surfaced by the BIOS tier (card 508245c0, branch feat/vm-bios-int): bweeper's draw_board sets es=0xB000 (MDA/text segment) and writes its board via es:[di] with di=BOARD_OFFSET (~0x8000+). Real hardware: physical 0xB8000-region video memory. Our flat CPU: the segment-override prefix is a no-op (by design, card d475eae9), so every draw lands at [edi] = low memory right after the binary — the game runs (budget) but renders nothing; matrix vga_bytes_changed=4000 comes only from the INT 10h mode-set clear, never from bweeper's own draws. Card d475eae9 deliberately deferred real-mode segmentation. Fix direction (design review first): cheapest faithful step is a segment-base window — latch DS/ES/FS/GS as <<4 bases when loaded from a 16-bit source's segment register (real-mode style), or translate es:offset to flat offset+0xB0000 at the _mem_operand level for the known video segments; must not change BITS 32 output or the flat syscall/kernel model. Evidence: scripts/compat/corpus/bweeper.asm draw_board (mov cx,0xb000 / mov es,cx / es:[di] writes); repro = run bweeper, diff mem[0x8000] vs mem[0xB8000].
APPROACH (2026-10-10, design review done — mechanism decided):
INVARIANT: real-mode segment registers are paragraph values; effective
address = (seg << 4) + offset. Card d475eae9 made the CPU emit the
override byte but treat it as a no-op (correct for BITS 32 flat code,
where prefixes never appear; wrong for BITS 16 real-mode code that
explicitly overrides). Existing assets confirmed by recon: 8E (mov
Sreg) already stores into cpu._segregs [ES,CS,SS,DS,FS,GS]; the
assembler already emits the prefix (mov es:[di],ax -> 26 66 89 07);
every corpus memory access goes through _decode_modrm.
MECHANISM: resolve the base at the single data-address choke point
_decode_modrm — NOT in _read8/_write8: instruction fetch
(_fetch_byte -> _read8) shares that accessor, and prefix consumption
happens BEFORE the opcode/modrm fetches, so a global application would
poison the fetch stream. Prefix loops (3 sites: _exec_one pre-66,
_exec_one post-66, _exec_16bit) set cpu._seg_base = segreg << 4;
_decode_modrm adds it to memory-operand addresses; _exec_one resets it
to 0 at every instruction boundary (no cross-instruction leak).
SCOPE GUARD: only ES/DS/FS/GS prefixes apply bases; CS/SS prefixes
stay no-ops (flat code + stack protection — the protected-mode boot
path stores 0x10 into every segment register; applying bases
unconditionally would shift any prefixed access by 0x100). Zero-blast-
radius invariants: (a) no prefixed instruction executed -> byte
identical; (b) segment register = 0 (all current tests + flat boot
paths) -> base 0 = today's behavior. Corpus surface measured: exactly
one prefixed operand form exists across all corpus files (es:[di] in
bweeper); mov Sreg appears in 4 files, all segs=0 or asm_gap programs.
bweeper's BOARD_OFFSET = 0x8542 -> physical 0xB0000+0x8542 = 0xB8542,
inside the harness's 4000-byte VGA window (board draws become visible
matrix evidence for the first time).
OUT OF SCOPE (follow-ups if corpus reaches them): string ops (movs/
stos) destination base — bootmine's stosw sits in an asm_gap program;
FS/GS beyond explicit prefixes; GDT descriptor bases (no real
protected mode here).
title: Flat-model VM drops segment bases — es=0xB000 video writes land at [edi] (bweeper board draws nowhere)

description: Observed 2026-10-09 while live-verifying a training fix: an external test suite (docstore test-session-id traffic, POST /training/start with invalid payloads -> 422, stop probes /training/jobs/99999999, -9 99999999, 99999/stop -> 404) runs against the shared live API on :8000 and issues POST /cancel-all?type=training — fired 19:14:21 and 19:36:28, killing verification jobs gc-verify-2 (step 8) and gc-verify-3 (step 8) mid-run. Impact: any session doing live training verification or any user's real training job gets killed by test runs; jobs self-mark cancelled (looks like a clean stop, root cause invisible without journal correlation). Fix direction: test suite should run against a dedicated instance/port (or skip /cancel-all in integration runs), or /cancel-all gains a scope guard (cancel only jobs created by the caller's session). Found during card fa33b9c1 live verification.
notes: ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-10-10, foreman investigation): the /cancel-all + bogus-ID stop bursts come from the SHELL REPL TEST SUITE hitting the LIVE :8000 over real HTTP. Chain: tests/core-py/test_shell_repl_more.py calls repl._cmd_kill('99999999'), _cmd_kill('-9 99999999'), _cmd_kill('invalid 1') (lines ~304/634/13998/19357) and ops cancel-all flows -> domain/shell/_internal/repl.py:_cmd_kill -> domain/shell/_internal/commands.py kill()/cancel_all_operations() (line 506 path='/cancel-all') -> _api_post(requests.post) -> get_api_base() defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000 (tests/conftest.py api_base_url fixture returns the same). The file mocks SOME calls (MagicMock patches) but not these HTTP paths, so every shell-test run cancels whatever real training jobs are running (bursts observed 2026-10-08 01:06 onward; killed verification jobs gc-verify-2/3/5 at steps 8/8/3). FIX DIRECTION (test isolation, not a scope guard): (a) hermetic-by-default — autouse fixture redirecting get_api_base() to an unroutable sentinel for non-slow core-py tests, with explicit live-marked tests opting in; verify no non-slow test currently relies on real responses (connection error != 404 body), or (b) patch _api_post/_api_get in the kill/ops tests specifically. (a) prevents the whole class. NOTE: shell test area saw recent commits (49b132eda) — check git status before touching; coordinate via this card.

LANDED + CLOSED (2026-10-11, foreman): d1c96d49e on fix/journal-append-race. Repo-side hermeticity delivered: autouse _hermetic_api fixture points get_api_base at http://127.0.0.1:9 (closed port, ConnectionRefused already handled -> error dict) in BOTH commands+config modules; TestHermeticApi guards pin it; the 2 tests that passed ONLY via live 404 text (test_kill_no_such, test_kill_invalid_signal) rewritten to mock ShellCommands.kill so the REPL error display is the subject. Evidence: full-file run 4005 passed/41 failed; all 41 re-run in pristine worktree under the identical dead-base plugin -> same 39 drift failures (pre-existing help/usage drift, card 33773fce family), net new failures ZERO; the 4 documented 99999999 stop probes now fail fast locally instead of POSTing to live :8000. SCOPE REMAINING (product decision, NOT done here): the /cancel-all killer was an EXTERNAL suite (docstore traffic, not in this repo) — repo test hermeticity cannot reach it; options: dedicated integration port for external suites, or /cancel-all scope guard (cancel only caller-session jobs). Surface to user; do not implement unilaterally.

[coord session 2026-10-11] Root-caused; fix is BLOCKED on the error-taxonomy branch's territory. Not built.

WHERE THE HARM COMES FROM, precisely:
  apps/api/server/routers/inference.py:3393  cancel_all_operations()
    - already has `auth_user: dict = Depends(require_auth_if_enabled)` in its signature
    - and NEVER USES IT in the body. It is fetched and dropped.
    - it calls mgr.cancel_all(op_type=...) which filters ONLY on op_type
  domain/infrastructure/_internal/cancel_manager.py:216  cancel_all()
    - filter is `op.status in (REGISTERED, RUNNING) and (op_type is None or op.op_type == op_type)`
    - no owner/tenant dimension exists at all
  => any caller, authenticated or not, can cancel every training op on the shared process.

WHY I DID NOT BUILD IT (this is the part that matters for whoever picks it up):
the scope guard needs operations to RECORD an owner at registration time, otherwise an
owner filter matches nothing and /cancel-all silently cancels nothing — strictly worse than
today, and it would look like a working fix in review. But every TRAINING registration site is
currently modified in the shared tree:
  apps/api/server/training/distill.py:126, router.py:363, legacy.py:89, from_feedback.py:117
All four are 'M' — the error-taxonomy session's live territory. Touching them would collide.

CLEAN AND READY for whoever has that branch: `Operation` already carries
`meta: dict[str, Any]` (cancel_manager.py:106), so an owner needs NO schema change —
register(meta={"owner": ...}) plus `cancel_all(op_type=None, *, owner=None)` filtering on
`op.meta.get("owner")`, with owner=None preserved for back-compat. The handler then passes
owner from auth_user. cancel_manager.py and inference.py are BOTH clean today; only the four
registration sites are contended.

ALSO WORTH FLAGGING: `require_auth_if_enabled` returns None when auth is disabled, so on this
box (auth off) there is no identity to scope by at all — a scope guard alone will not stop the
reported traffic. That argues for the card's OTHER fix direction (test suite against a dedicated
instance/port) as the part that actually stops the bleeding, with the scope guard as defence in
depth once auth is on.

description: Slice of card 33773fce (refactor-drift backlog): 24/24 failures in tests/core-py/test_kernel_devices.py, one root cause. Timeline: tests written 2026-08-03 (ca4603011) against per-driver open/read/write + table read_fd/write_fd/ioctl_fd/close_fd/device_count + DeviceHandle-returning open(); 96b0d69d1 (2026-09-03, 'Baseboard: bit-based DeviceTable + DeviceDriver gates') rewrote kernel_devices.py to ioctl-only dispatch over an int-fd bitmap and turned DeviceType into bit flags (INFERENCE=1..INPUT=32, CUSTOM=0) and never touched the tests. Red ever since: 5x FakeDevice missing open/is_open, 7x DeviceTable missing read_fd/write_fd/ioctl_fd/close_fd/device_count, 2x DeviceDriver missing read/write, plus stale enum values and open() returning an int rather than DeviceHandle/None. Verified: no production caller of the removed API anywhere in domain/ or apps/. Plan: port the file to the current contract (ioctl answers SyscallResult, int fds, -1 on error, stats() for counts), and restore three invariants the rewrite silently dropped: (A) DeviceTable.unregister returns False for an unregistered name (pre-rewrite contract; the old test asserted it; register() is honest so unregister() should be too); (B) unregister frees fds bound to the removed device - alias-aware, since 1a2fb8588 aliases share one driver and the surviving name owns the fd - else a dangling fd keeps dispatching ioctls into an unregistered device (the old code closed the device here for exactly that reason); (C) DeviceManager.register must not clobber _devices[name] when the table rejects a duplicate (it writes the mirror before validating, so get() returns a device the table never registered). Out of scope: test_devices.py + test_devices_more.py are green.

description:
# Summary

Two independent buckets from the cleanup sweep, both "test↔implementation
drift" but with **one genuine source bug** hiding in the second bucket.

| File | Before | After | Root cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/core-py/test_data_import.py` | 26 failed / 188 passed | **214 passed** | 3 causes, all test-side drift + live network |
| `tests/core-py/test_cpu_topology.py` | 6 failed / 42 passed | **48 passed** | 1 cause, **real source bug** |

Runtime for `test_data_import.py` also fell **97.4s → 18.2s (5.4x)** once the
live network calls were removed.

---

# Part 1 — `test_data_import.py` (26 failures, 3 root causes)

## A. Wrong dispatch class patched — 6 tests

`import_data()` dispatches by source type:

```
github      -> RepoImporter().import_from_github()
url         -> URLImporter().import_from_url()
huggingface -> HuggingFaceImporter().download_dataset()
local       -> DataImporter().import_from_local()
```

`TestImportData` patched `DataImporter.<method>` for **all** of them, so only
`local` was actually mocked. The github/url/hf tests ran the real
implementation → a live `git clone` (exit 128) and live HTTP fetches.

Fix: `_patch_method()` now takes the target class, and each test patches the
class `import_data` really dispatches to.

## B. `ISBNImporter` signature drift — 12 tests

`_fetch_gutenberg_text()` gained a third `isbn` argument (its real caller at
`data_import.py:1103` passes all three). The tests still called it with two and
monkeypatched it with 2-arg lambdas → `TypeError`.

While fixing the arity it surfaced a second, worse problem: `import_from_isbn()`
checks the **direct ISBN endpoint first** (`get_by_isbn`, a live OpenLibrary
call) and only then the mocked `search`. So:

- `test_import_not_found` mocked `search -> []` but `get_by_isbn` hit live
  OpenLibrary. Because `0306406152` is a real book, the import **succeeded**,
  flipping `success=False` to `True` depending on network state.
- `test_fetch_gutenberg_no_search_terms` had **no `fake_urlopen` at all** — a
  bare call straight to live Gutendex.

Fix: force `get_by_isbn -> None` where the test intends the mocked `search` to
decide, add the missing `fake_urlopen`, and add the third argument. The
`test_fetch_gutenberg_success` response queue was reordered to preserve its
original intent (ISBN probe misses -> title search hits -> download) now that
the probe consumes the first mocked response.

One stale expectation corrected: `test_import_not_found` asserted the dataset
directory is created on failure, but `import_from_isbn()` returns **before**
`mkdir`. Not creating litter for a failed import is the better behaviour, so the
assertion now checks the directory does *not* exist.

## C. Brittle exact-URL assertion — 1 test

`test_search_title` pinned the whole OpenLibrary URL including the `fields=`
list, which has since been deliberately extended (subject, publisher,
physical_format, number_of_pages_median). Rewritten to assert the stable parts
(prefix + required fields present) so the next field addition doesn't break it.

Also corrected 8 `_is_isbn` assertions that expected an `isbn:` prefix. That
prefix is OpenLibrary **search-query** syntax; `_is_isbn` returns normalized
digits because its output feeds the `/isbn/{id}.json` endpoint, where a prefix
would corrupt the URL.

---

# Part 2 — `cpu_topology.py` (6 failures, **real source bug**)

## Root cause: hardware probes could crash the process

Six `except` clauses in `domain/infrastructure/_internal/cpu_topology.py`
protected the narrow tuples `(FileNotFoundError, ValueError)` or
`(CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError, ValueError)` around `lscpu`,
`/proc/cpuinfo`, sysfs reads and `sysctl`.

But `subprocess.check_output()` and `open()` also raise `PermissionError` and
generic `OSError` (unexecutable binary, EINTR, EACCES, restricted `/proc` in a
container). Those escaped the handler and **crashed detection**, even though
every one of these functions has a fallback right there — `return 0.0`,
`return 1`, `physical = max(1, logical // 2)`.

The file was also internally inconsistent: `_detect_numa` already caught
`OSError` for its own sysfs fallback (line 207) and `_has_cgroup_cpuset` caught
`OSError` (line 266), while the `lscpu`/`/proc/cpuinfo` calls one function over
did not.

Fix: all 7 probe sites now use `except Exception` with an explicit
`# best-effort probe: degrade, never crash` marker. This matches the precedent
the same module already set in `_parse_sysctl_string` (`except Exception:
return None`). These feed a scheduler sizing hint — crashing the process over a
CPU-frequency reading is strictly worse than returning `0.0`.

## Blast radius

Only consumer is `resource_manager.py`, which uses `detect_topology()` as a
`field(default_factory=...)` and as `topology or detect_topology()`. It expects
a **return value**, never an exception — so broadening the handlers makes that
caller strictly more reliable. No caller depended on the exception escaping.
Verified: `test_resource_manager.py` 35 passed.

---

# Verification

- `test_data_import.py`: **214 passed**, run twice to confirm non-flaky
- `test_cpu_topology.py`: **48 passed**
- `test_resource_manager.py`: **35 passed** (consumer of the changed probes)
- Combined touched suites (`data_import`, `vector_store`, `knowledge_memory`,
  `knowledge_ops`): **401 passed, 0 failed**
- `ruff check .`: all checks passed

# Files changed

- `tests/core-py/test_data_import.py`
- `domain/infrastructure/_internal/cpu_topology.py`
title: 32 stale/non-hermetic tests fixed: data_import (26) + cpu_topology probe crash (6)

description:
Commit 1eb96c08a (feat/caret-core). Sixth bucket of the
test_shell_repl_more.py tail — 4 tests, 3 causes, test-side only (zero
production lines, no behaviour delta).

## 1. Phantom glyph (1 test)

    before  assert "̓" in result   (U+0343 COMBINING GREEK KORONIS)
    after   assert "λ" in result   (U+03BB)

Pytest renders the failure as `assert '̓' in 'λ'`, which looks like a missing
accent. The needle is U+0343, which is in ZERO production files and in ZERO
commits (`git log -S --all` empty) — it could never have passed on any
branch. Test name/intent kept; only the glyph corrected.

U+0343 does not survive tool round-tripping (a direct edit failed to match),
so the swap was done by `.splitwork/fix_render_glyph.py`, which builds both
strings with chr(0x0343)/chr(0x03BB) and aborts unless exactly one
occurrence exists.

## 2. Mock broad enough to kill the error formatter (2 tests)

    before  patch("builtins.__import__", side_effect=ImportError("no module"))
    after   patch.dict(sys.modules, {"domain.infrastructure._internal.model_protector": None})

The question was good ("if protect's dependency is unimportable, does the
user see an Error?") but breaking EVERY import also broke the import the
error handler needs:

    repl.py:2768  self._print(self._format_error(e, "protect"))
    repl.py:4282      from domain.shell._internal.error import format_error   <- mocked too

The formatter's lazy import raised inside the except block, so the original
ImportError never reached the user and the test died with an uncaught
exception instead of a wrong message. Narrowing to sys.modules[...]=None
fails exactly the target dependency (import raises "None in sys.modules")
while leaving error.py importable = the scenario the test means.

FOLLOW-UP (real): `_format_error` can still throw from inside an except
handler if error.py is unimportable. "An error handler must not be able to
raise" — production question, recorded not papered over.

Guards deliberately untouched: 3 other builtins.__import__ patches
(9061/9098/9211, `side_effect=mock_import`) + the ImportError("no curses")
one (20261) — different mechanism, replaceAll scoped to the exact
"no module" string so only the 2 failing tests matched.

## 3. Stale completion prefix (1 test)

    before  repl._complete("dev", 0)   -> None
    after   repl._complete("mode", 0)

Assertion is `result is not None or _ext_cmds == {}`. There are 18 ext
commands and NONE starts with "dev" (starts with "mod": ['models']). Test is
named test_complete_ext_cmd — it wants to prove ext completion works, so the
prefix was corrected to one that exists rather than the assertion weakened.

## Correction owed to 7f7602e81

Its message claimed e5208a8c9's `lsdev`/`devices` were "already present
here". Half wrong: `devices in COMMANDS = False`, `lsdev = True`, and
`_cmd_devices` does not exist. Only lsdev ever reached this branch. Recorded
here per the correction-note precedent (740ea0b26), not by rewriting history.
Registering `devices` would also satisfy the tab test, but it adds an
undocumented user-facing command — out of scope for a test-only bucket.

## Result

    8 -> 4 failed;  4077 passed;  36 skipped;  total 4117 unchanged
    4 targets + 4 guards  8 passed in 36.51s
    ruff + py_compile clean
    full run 5 failed / 4076 passed / 444s at load average 35.59 —
    cleared exactly the 4, 1 NEW = TestCmdDuDeeper3::test_du_no_args which
    passes 2/2 in isolation (6.81s). Known _execute_single system-binary
    flake under load, not a regression (an earlier run in the same window
    showed 6, both du tests flaking).

Campaign: 18 commits (1b78df86e -> ... -> 1eb96c08a).
Failure trajectory: 81 -> 69 -> 41 -> 26 -> 23 -> 21 -> 17 -> 12 -> 8 -> 4.

## Remaining 4 — both need decisions, not patches

**kill (2)** `test_kill_no_such`, `test_kill_invalid_signal`
`_cmd_kill` error branch prints `[kill] Exception: HTTP 404` but never sets
_last_exit_code, so a FAILED kill exits 0. The one-line fix is NOT safe: 9
passing tests assert exit == 0 after killing a nonexistent job (305, 635,
5199, 5203, 13489, 13493, 14006, 14010, 17116). The suite contradicts itself
9-vs-2 — either retarget the 9 (shell-correct) or retarget the 2.

**vmrun (2)** `test_vmrun_built_in_count`, `test_vmrun_piped_input`
Documented built-in `count` (listed by --list) dies with
`unknown opcode 0x62 at EIP=0x101FF0`; a well-formed piped x86 program dies
with `read8 out of bounds at 0x69590027`. Points at assembler/VM, not the
shell wrapper — own investigation warranted.

description:
Card 17584ac9. Investigation complete; fix was written, verified, and then
**explicitly declined** ("Don't land; revert the whole change") — all three
files were reverted and HEAD stayed at 1eb96c08a. Recording the root cause so
it is not re-derived from scratch.

## Root cause (verified, not hypothesised)

`_CUDABackend.matmul` decided whether to convert its inputs with duck typing:

    self._cp.asarray(a) if not hasattr(a, "device") else a

That guard was written to mean "already on the device, don't re-wrap".
**numpy >= 2.0 gives every `ndarray` a `.device` attribute** (the array-API
device attribute; it is `'cpu'` for host memory). Verified here:

    numpy 2.5.3
    hasattr(np.zeros((4,4), dtype=np.float32), "device") -> True
    np.zeros((4,4), dtype=np.float32).device              -> 'cpu'

So the guard was False for plain numpy input, conversion was skipped, and
numpy went straight into `cp.matmul`, which raises:

    TypeError: expected cupy._core.core._ndarray_base, got numpy.ndarray

SloNet catches that in `_matmul` (`domain/training/_internal/slonet.py:952`)
and falls back to `np.matmul`. Net effect: **the GPU was never used for any
matmul**, plus a per-call WARNING that floods journald and, on handlers that
retain records (pytest caplog, memory/queue handlers), pins the caught
exception's traceback frames and keeps that matmul's arrays alive.

4 affected sites, all in `_CUDABackend.matmul`:
lines 990, 991 (fp32 arm) and 995, 996 (fp16 arm).

Two byte-identical copies carry the code — they are NOT symlinks (different
inodes, same size/mtime):
  domain/slolib/_internal/gpu.py
  packages/core-py/domains/slolib/gpu/__init__.py
Any future fix must edit both or the dual tree desyncs.

Note: the older `domain/training/_internal/gpu/accelerator.py`
`_CUDAAccelerator.matmul` converts unconditionally (`self._cp.asarray(a)`),
so it does NOT have this bug. Only slolib's backend does — and
`_get_accelerator()` tries slolib first (`slonet.py:236`).

## Why no test caught it

`tests/.../test_slolib_gpu.py` already had `TestCudaWithFakeCupy` with a
numpy-backed cupy stand-in, but the stand-in's `matmul` did
`np.matmul(cls._val(a), cls._val(b))`, which **accepts numpy input**. Real
cupy is type-strict and raises. A permissive fake cannot model a type-strict
boundary, so the broken guard was invisible — the existing
`test_cuda_matmul_with_fake_cupy` passed while production was dead.

A faithful fake needs three things the current one lacks:
1. type-strict `matmul` (reject numpy with cupy's message),
2. an `ndarray` attribute (real cupy exposes `cupy.ndarray`),
3. idempotent `asarray` on device arrays of matching dtype.

## What the reverted fix did

Introduced `_to_cupy(arr, dtype=None)` using nominal typing
(`isinstance(arr, self._cp.ndarray)`) instead of the 4 inline duck-type
checks, so the invariant is stated once.

Verified on branch `feat/gpu-matmul-numpy2-device` (never committed):
  - 5 GPU suites, baseline 114F/278P -> after 115F/279P
  - NEW: exactly 1 (`test_cuda_matmul_with_fake_cupy`); FIXED: 0
  - the 1 NEW is not a regression in the fix: that test asserts `atol=1e-4`
    on the **fp16** arm, which only held because the broken guard also skipped
    the dtype conversion, so fp16 never engaged and the result was fp32.
    Genuine fp16 error measured at 8.6e-4, vs 0.0 for fp32.
  - ruff + py_compile clean.

## Second-order effect worth knowing

`_Accelerator._prec_benchmark` (`gpu.py:200`) calls `self.matmul(a, b)` with
numpy arrays to choose fp16 vs fp32. Under the bug it measured fp32 **twice**,
so `set_precision("auto")` was deciding from a benchmark that never exercised
fp16. Fixing the guard would also have made auto-precision honest.

## Measured: is engaging the GPU even worth it?

GTX 1050 (cupy 14.2.0), `.splitwork/gpu_wip/bench_gpu_vs_numpy.py`:

    shape      out_elems   numpy(ms)   cuda(ms)    ratio
    (64x64)         4,096      0.032       0.929     0.03x  <- CPU faster
    (116x141)      13,456     35.401       2.094    16.91x
    (256x256)      65,536     36.450       3.120    11.68x
    (512x512)     262,144     59.900       5.891    10.17x
    (1024x1024) 1,048,576    136.900      20.218     6.77x
    (2048x2048) 4,194,304    697.545      41.018    17.01x

Caveat: load average was 26 during measurement, so the numpy column is
contention-bound (a 3x larger matmul showing 100x the time is BLAS thread
thrash, not compute). The cuda column was stable across two runs. The signal
that does not depend on load: below the 16384-element dispatch threshold the
GPU is ~30x **slower** because host->device->host conversion dominates, which
is exactly why that threshold exists and should not be lowered.

## Decision

Not landed, by explicit user decision. The GPU-vs-CPU numerics change, the
fp16 engagement, and the auto-precision honesty fix were judged too risky to
take in one change. Revisit as its own card if wanted: the honest sequencing
is (1) land the type-strict fake-cupy fidelity fixes as a pure test change,
(2) then the `_to_cupy` guard with the fp16 tolerance corrected, each with its
own gate.
title: [DONE 2026-10-10] GPU matmul root cause: numpy>=2.0 ndarray.device defeats hasattr guard — GPU never engaged (fix written, verified, DECLINED, reverted)

  await waitFor(() => expect(mocks.mockDecode).toHaveBeenCalledWith([3,12,99]))

THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS, STRANDED on feat/device-contract /
feat/npu-slnc-only / fix/gpu-accelerator-linalg-api — never an ancestor of main.

DEFECT (verified live in main, not guessed):
  git grep -c _npu_op <integration> -- domain/shell/_internal/vm_devices.py
  -> 0, i.e. main still calls self._npu.<op> directly.

The VM-to-NPU bridge reaches for self._npu.<op> directly. The kernel NPU that
runtime.py wires in implements only 4 of the 25 ops, has no __getattr__, and
exposes everything else through ioctl() -> SyscallResult. So 21 of 25 ops raise
AttributeError in production — including all 7 ops NPUVMDevice's own docstring
promises (load_model, tokenize, generate, detokenize, embed, forward,
unload_model). The FIRST thing any guest program does — DEV_OPEN npu / DEV_CALL
load_model — faults.

Second defect in the same site: _load_model calls load_file, which exists on
NEITHER side (the NPU has load(path, name); test doubles have
load_model(name, source); load_file lives only on weight_loader.py:953), and the
argument order was inverted relative to both.

THE FIX: _npu_op(op, *args) as the single choke point —
  1. ioctl when the op has a _IOCTL_MAP entry and the NPU exposes ioctl
     (returns the SyscallResult shape every op already expects);
  2. else a same-named method, which keeps every test double working unchanged;
  3. else DeviceFault, so a guest sees a device error, never a leaked
     AttributeError.

APPLICABILITY (checked): the merge-base is f27654e54 and main has NOT changed
vm_devices.py since it, so a cherry-pick of just this sha should apply cleanly —

description:
PRODUCTION BUG (repo-root off-by-one) — found 2026-10-08, DBs land outside the repo.

FILE: apps/api/server/infrastructure/db_pool.py:24

    def _get_repo_root() -> Path:
        global _REPO_ROOT
        if _REPO_ROOT is None:
            _REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5]   # <-- off by one

DEPTH PROOF (file = apps/api/server/infrastructure/db_pool.py)
    parents[4] = .../sloughGPT        <- actual repo root
    parents[5] = .../Default Project  <- PARENT of the repo

CONSEQUENCE: split-brain between metadata and bytes
- db_pool writes every MogDB to   <repo-parent>/data/<db_name>
  (+ its _json sync dir, default <name>_mogdb -> <name>_json)
- FilesRouter.UPLOADS_DIR uses parents[4] correctly -> <repo>/data/uploads
=> file bytes in-repo, file metadata out-of-repo. Verified: the live uploads
   journal sits at Default Project/data/uploads_mogdb/files.journal.jsonl
   (1,046,912 bytes) while <repo>/data/uploads_mogdb/ holds a stale Oct-5 copy.
- 4 _mogdb dirs exist in the parent, 14 in the repo: two divergent data homes.

WHY NOT A ONE-LINE FIX
Flipping to parents[4] redirects every database to <repo>/data/, which makes the
app stop seeing the data currently in <repo-parent>/data/. That is a migration,
not a patch: needs a move plan + a backup + a decision about which tree is canonical.

DECISION (user, 2026-10-08): file as a card, do NOT change it in this branch.

SUGGESTED PATH
1. decide canonical data home (in-repo data/ is gitignored, so it is safe)
2. back up <repo-parent>/data/
3. change parents[5] -> parents[4]
4. move <repo-parent>/data/* to <repo>/data/ (no overwrites without backup)
5. verify GET /files lists pre-existing uploads afterward
title: db_pool _get_repo_root uses parents[5] — DBs written outside the repo

description:
Landed on `fix/tui-live-harness-stream-parser`.

- `6b4d7f83f` — harness: `_Screen.feed()` as a true stream parser (split CSI,
  split UTF-8, lone ESC at a chunk boundary) + fingerprint quiescence instead
  of a pessimistic fixed settle.
- `4222463a9` — production: GraphicsEngine becomes the sole screen owner.

Root causes (three, all real):

1. `GraphicsEngine.render()` diffed `_front_buffer` against `_back_buffer`,
   which is never updated from the front buffer, so no erase was ever emitted
   when a layer shrank; `_prev_buffer` is the frame actually presented.
2. ncurses cleared the screen behind the engine's back, which a diff-only
   engine cannot observe — the old diff-vs-blank engine repaired this *by
   accident* by repainting everything every tick. Curses is gone from
   `tui_repl.py` entirely (`_RawTerminal`, `_Win`, local KEY_* at ncurses'
   values); ICRNL deliberately preserved so LF-based submit still fires.
3. `_render_status` lost the `[OUTPUT]/[LOG]` switch and the `SCROLL n` word
   in `9f348d0c9` — a commit whose message claims a cognitive->cognition
   rename but which actually ported the status bar. It printed OUTPUT in both
   branches, so PgUp/Ctrl+O could never report scroll or log focus.

Plus a test-side fix: `_Screen.flat_text()` normalises pane fill (`░`) so
assertions match logical text rather than the stale input-row echo that only
survived because erases were missing. No assertion was weakened.

Gates: 28 failed/14 passed -> **42 passed/0 failed**; ruff clean; mypy 25 -> 19
errors, none new; `benchmark_graphics` warm render -22%, write+render -48%;
steady terminal traffic ~370KB/s -> ~52B/s, `clears` 2 -> 1.
title: TUI live tests: harness stream fix, curses removal, render erase bug

description:
Landed as `59b15ef36` on `fix/app-planner-md-notes`. **Premise corrected while
fixing it** — the original description was directionally right but the mechanism
was wrong, and the difference decided the design.

Original claim: "app-planner reads notes.journal.jsonl, so sync is a silent no-op
for the 169 md notes." In fact `PlannerStore._notes_dir` resolves to
`<root>/.dev-notes`, which holds a journal of 122 notes and where sync works
fine. It was never a no-op in general — app-planner was pointed at a *different
directory* than the one AGENTS.md designates, and `--notes-dir ~/.config/dev-notes`
was still silent because PlannerStore parses a JSONL journal and nothing else.

Measured 2026-10-11, the two stores are **disjoint, not duplicated**:
journal 122 notes (uuid ids) vs markdown 170 notes (date-stem ids), **0 id
overlap, 4 title overlap**. So this is not consolidation — two separate note
sets, ~292 notes, only the second documented.

The trap: `update_note`/`delete_note` round-trip `_read_notes()` ->
`_write_notes(notes)`. The obvious fix (markdown into `_read_notes`) would have
copied all 170 `.md` notes into the journal on the next write and silently merged
the stores. Read the write paths before extending a read path.

What landed:
- read-only `_read_markdown_notes()`, merged via `_read_all_notes()` into
  list/get/search — and therefore `sync()`, which reads via `list_notes()`;
- `_read_notes` untouched, so the three write round-trips still see only the
  journal and the stores can never merge by accident;
- reused `core.Note.from_markdown` (a *different* dataclass from `store.Note` —
  it carries `author`) rather than writing a second parser; adapted the carrier;
- fixed `from_markdown`'s tag parse, the path this activates: it split on commas
  alone, so the dominant real format `tags: [a, b, c]` yielded `["[a","b","c]"]`
  and those brackets travelled into board card tags on sync. Bare `a,b` still
  parses.

Proven, not asserted: `<root>/.dev-notes` has no `*.md`, and `sync()` on a copy
of the real 1117-card board reported **added=0, updated=0** — byte-identical.
The same run pointed at `~/.config/dev-notes` found all 170 notes and would add
**151** cards. **Not applied** — that is a migration (70 already done, 25 active
cards flooding a shared queue), tracked on the follow-on card.

Gates: 12 passed (9 new + the atomic-write guard); packages/app-planner's own
suite 206 passed; tests/contract 9 passed; ruff check + format clean; mypy 0 -> 0.

Backing note: `~/.config/dev-notes/2026-10-11-app-planner-md-notes.md`.
title: app-planner could not read the notes AGENTS.md calls the source of truth

description:
Measured 2026-10-11. `python scripts/check_feature_tags.py` reports "Total: 702
feature-tagged files" and exits 0. The real number is 12.

  git grep -lE "FEATURE:\s*[a-z][a-z-]+" -- '*.py' | wc -l   ->  12
  same, unique feature names                                 ->  11

ROOT CAUSE: find_feature_tagged_files() does `root.rglob("*.py")` from the repo root and excludes
only __pycache__, node_modules and scripts/. It does NOT exclude the ~20 `.wt-*` git worktrees
that live inside the repo root, each a full checkout — so every tagged file is counted once per
worktree. slo_manager.py alone appears ~18 times in its own output.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the guard that exists to "prevent deletion of tagged files unless
explicitly overridden" (its own docstring). A guard that counts the worktree copies as if they
were distinct files will happily pass while the ONE tracked file it was protecting gets deleted —
the copies are untracked and vanish with their worktree. It reports green while measuring the
wrong thing, which is worse than not having the check.

FIX DIRECTION: iterate tracked files only (`git ls-files '*.py'`) instead of rglobbing the
working tree — that matches the guard's actual purpose (protect files under version control) and
makes worktrees invisible by construction. Add a test asserting the count matches git, so the
number can never silently drift again.

description:
Landed as `dadfad34e` on `fix/slonet-benchmark-gates`. Follow-on to card
`a25e490b` (whose id is duplicated on the board with unrelated content merged
into one copy, so this work is recorded here instead of mutating that record).

`benchmark_slonet.py` prints "Passed: X/Y" and writes
`data/eval_results/slonet_benchmark.json`, so every TestResult read as a gate.
Four were not:

1. `accelerator_speed` — `passed=True` as a literal: PASS at any ratio,
   including an accelerator slower than numpy. Now gates on the invariant it
   already measured (`speedup > 1.0`), informational when `acc.name == "cpu"`
   because there the accelerator IS numpy.
2. `accelerator_matmul_crossover` — same literal. Now gates on the condition
   its own diagnostic already spelled out in prose: `crossover <=
   dispatch_gate`, with `crossover=None` treated as the worst case, not a pass.
3. `lstm_forward_backward_speed` — same literal, but a raw seconds_per_step
   with no baseline: no invariant exists. Declared `informational=True` rather
   than handed an invented threshold, which would have swapped a blind gate
   for a flaky one.
4. **`test_accelerator_matmul_crossover` was never called from `run_all()`** —
   the dispatch-gate check had never once executed, while looking like
   coverage in the file listing. Wired in.

`print_summary()` now counts gates, and `main()` derives its JSON summary from
the same `gate_counts()` helper so the two cannot drift — the file said 8/8
while the terminal said 7/7 gates. Measurements print `○ MEASURE`, not
`✓ PASS`.

Measured (GTX 1050 + cuPy 14.2): accelerator_speed **17.4x** cuda vs numpy;
crossover **16,384** elements against a dispatch gate of 16,384 — the gate is
well placed, and is now checked rather than asserted.

`tests/contract/test_benchmark_gates.py` (test-first, red on exactly the three
named offenders) holds both directions: no literal `passed=True` outside a
declared measurement, and **no benchmark method may be unreachable from
`run_all()`** — the generalisable guard that would have caught defect 4
immediately.

Gates: 8 passed (new) + 17 passed (whole `tests/contract/`); benchmark exit 0
at 7/7 gates + 1 measurement with the JSON summary agreeing; ruff check and
format clean; mypy 1 -> 1 error, none new.

Backing note: `~/.config/dev-notes/2026-10-11-slonet-benchmark-gates.md`.

& Transport Rule requires naming the boundary before code, and this is a new endpoint.

BOUNDARY: web/mobile run in the browser (a different process), so a transport crossing IS
justified — this is not a same-process function call. But it must be one descriptor-projected
route, not an endpoint-per-feature, and it must not become a generic flag switchyard.

- Evaluator stays a sync in-memory read in domain/shared. The refresh fetch lives at the app

BLOCKED ON the same product call as roadmap step 1: with 25 of 26 flags unread, publishing a
flag surface mostly publishes an inventory of intent. Decide wire-or-delete first, otherwise
the endpoint serves a list of capabilities that do not exist.

description:
PROBLEM — a recurring, silent regression class. A "converge X to main — was N
lines stale" style commit (single-parent, NOT a merge — verified 074475d26 has
one parent) wholesale-overwrites a tree from a stale snapshot and silently
reverts fixes that landed in the interim. Proven instances this session:

  1. 074475d26 ("converge packages/avion to main, 3547 lines stale") reverted
     b94798cbc's structured-field logger fix back to a positional %s f-string
     → latent TypeError. Restored 443ad24e0. NO test locked it, which is WHY
     the clobber succeeded silently (verified: grep across tests/ + packages/
     avion finds zero assertions on that line).
  2. 81616a6f7 sweep silently deleted EmbeddingConfig.api_key/base_url/
     _sync_openai_alias (card ff9ef505) — restored 61831dc4d, locked by
     0e9fab853 (11 tests in tests/test_embedding_config.py).
  3. 0a29d5c6e deleted commands/monitor.py but left the import in
     apps/cli/src/groups/train.py → live ModuleNotFoundError (card 8182563a),
     fixed cc7a5e3ee, locked by 18 tests in tests/cli/test_logs_unification.py.
  4. Board rows lost to stale-base board merges (5311698a, 8182563a, 7e2af9fe,
     e8fd60d4 all still read todo while fix+closure were already in tip).

ROOT OBSERVATION: the fixes that survived are exactly the ones WITH a locking
test; the one that got re-clobbered (avion) had NONE. The test file IS the
guard — it lives in a path the converging branch typically does not touch, so
it survives and goes red in CI.

WHY A SCRIPT DETECTOR WAS REJECTED: the obvious alternative — a
scripts/check_clobber.py that git-scans for "commit reverted a line a prior
fix added" — needs git history (shallow CI clones break it), a heuristic to
decide "this line was a fix", and would emit noisy false positives. The
regression-lock test file is this repo's established idiom (test_embedding_
config.py and test_logs_unification.py are already exactly this), needs zero
new CI wiring (the existing "Root tests" job runs `pytest tests/`), and fails
loudly with a message naming the card + sha.

PLAN
  - New tests/test_regression_locks.py: TABLE-DRIVEN registry of
    (lock_id, path, must_contain[], must_not_contain[], cite) so adding a
    lock is one row, not one file. Each entry cites the card id + fix sha +
    the clobbering sha so the provenance is self-documenting.
  - Lock the known-unlocked fix FIRST: avion structured-field session log
    (443ad24e0, clobbered by 074475d26). Assert the fixed form is present AND
    the clobbered (positional %s) form is absent.
  - Add rows for the already-locked fixes as cheap cross-pins (import-free
    source-level checks) so a future sweep that DELETES the locking test file
    itself still trips the central registry.
  - Prove the guard works: mutate the source back to the clobbered form in a
    scratch copy and show the test goes RED with the citation in the message.
  - Run lint + the full new file under the project env.

FOLLOW-UP (not this card): a pre-push scripts/check_clobber.py heuristic for
UNKNOWN future clobbers — registry locks only protect what we know about.
title: Regression-lock guard: pin clobber-prone fixes as executable assertions so stale-base overwrites fail CI

description:
Discovered by the site-doctor probe (`1c5abc300`, card e8fd60d4).
**2 of 4 fixed. The other 2 are not bugs — measured below.** Branch
`fix/site-doctor-dead-routes`.

| route | root cause | state |
|---|---|---|
| `/phoneme/languages` | `supported_languages` is a `@property` returning `list[str]`; the handler called it `()` -> `'list' object is not callable` -> `E_LANGUAGES_FAILED`. Introduced already-wrong by `5717e1f5f`; wrong on `main` too. | **FIXED `1c5e36f8a`** |
| `/providers` | non-JSON `provider.metadata` is well-formed inside the handler, so the per-provider guard never fires — it fails later in the response encoder, outside the guard -> `E_SERIALIZATION`. | **FIXED `230adc605`** |
| `/registry/artifacts` | **not a bug.** ~7s = filesystem walk. See below. | measured, needs a decision |
| `/registry/verify` | **not a bug.** ~20s = hashing all 3.985 GB, most of it unverifiable. See below. | measured, needs a decision |

## Correction to the probe's original labels

The probe first labelled these "slow, not dead" and "genuinely hangs, no
response in >15s". Both labels were wrong, from a single cold measurement.
Four warm runs each, and direct-vs-gateway isolation:

    /registry/artifacts  :8000 -> 6.95s 7.12s   :8080 -> 7.12s 7.07s
    /registry/verify     :8000 -> 17.6s 19.6s   :8080 -> 19.3s 18.1s
    control /health      :8000 -> 0.0068s       :8080 -> 0.0003s

They answer every time. The gateway costs ~0.1s, so it was never implicated.
The app itself is slow, and reproducibly so — 7s and 20s, not "a hang".

## /registry/artifacts — O(tree), not O(artifacts)

93 artifacts, 3.985 GB, scanned in ~7s = **75 ms per artifact for a listing**.
`list_artifacts` calls one iterator per kind (6 kinds), and those iterators do
`rglob("*")` / `iterdir()` over the scan roots, so the cost tracks the size of
the trees walked, not the number of artifacts returned. Nothing is hashed here
— it is pure metadata I/O.

The registry is also **not worktree-neutral**: the same call from a worktree
sees 23 artifacts / 0.02 GB, from the main checkout 93 / 3.985 GB, because
part of the root set resolves via `repo_root()`. Two servers started from two
worktrees will report different registries for the same machine.

## /registry/verify — 20s to verify 13 artifacts

`verify()` returns `{'ok': 13, 'mismatch': 2, 'missing': 0, 'unverified': 78}`
for a 3.985 GB payload. **78 of 93 artifacts had no baseline to check against**,
and they still cost the full hash.

The cause is a policy split *inside one function*:

  - `kind == "download"` (line 554): `if expected:` — hashes **only** when a
    baseline exists.
  - the general file case (line 574): `actual = _sha256_file(path)` runs
    **unconditionally**, then line 575 checks `if expected is None` and returns
    "unverified". The hash is computed and thrown into the response body
    ("hash reported for the record", per the docstring).

So it is intentional, but the two branches of the same function disagree about
whether an unverifiable file should be hashed at all.

**The live risk is not slowness, it is a ceiling.** `/registry/verify` is
O(total bytes); the gateway caps at 30s and already returned **504 on the
first cold run**. At 3.985 GB it takes 20s. Double the artifacts and every
call 504s.

## Decisions needed (not taken unilaterally)

Per the endpoint rule, these are design calls, not fixes:

1. `/registry/verify` — hash only what has a baseline (matches the download
   branch, cuts ~20s -> ~3s), or bound it (`limit`/`kind`) and move it onto the
   existing **operations/CancelManager** framework, which already exists for
   exactly this class of long-running work. Leaving it as a blocking GET means
   it silently becomes a guaranteed 504 as artifacts accumulate.
2. `/registry/artifacts` — is 7s for a listing acceptable, or should the walk
   be cached/invalidated (the registry is explicitly "the filesystem stays the
   source of truth", so a cache needs an invalidation story)?

## The recurring lesson (both fixed routes)

Neither bug was untested. Both were covered by tests that could not fail:

- **`/phoneme/languages`** — `test_phoneme_router.py` drove the route through a
  bare `MagicMock`, which accepts any attribute access *and* any call, so
  `engine.supported_languages()` returned another mock. The mock also encoded
  the wrong shape, so the passing assertion checked a payload no client ever
  receives.
- **`/providers`** — `test_list_providers_returns_dict` asserted
  `isinstance(body["data"], dict)` against an **empty registry**: the loop body
  never ran, `data` was `{}`, and `{}` is a dict.

A mock or an empty registry turns a boundary test into a tautology. The seam is
where the bugs live, and it is exactly the seam the tests abstracted away.

Both A/B-proven (fix stashed -> new test fails, old tests stay green):

    /phoneme/languages   broken: 2 failed, 15 passed   |  fixed: 17 passed
    /providers           broken: 1 failed, 1 passed    |  fixed: 2 passed

## Secondary: the 500s are silent by design

`E_SERIALIZATION` has two raise sites (`exception_handlers.py:200`,
`middleware.py:567`) and both emit the **same generic message**, attaching
`detail` only `if logger.isEnabledFor(DEBUG)`. At the default log level the
cause is never written down — which is why the live `/providers` 500 named
nothing and took a reproduction to pin.

Gates: `test_phoneme_router.py` 17 + `test_phoneme_api.py`/`test_unified_phoneme_encoder.py`
103 + `test_inference_router.py` 54, all passed; ruff clean.
notes:
STATUS 2026-10-11 — 3 of 4 routes FIXED and landed; the remaining 2 are NOT dead, and the
card's description of them was wrong. All numbers below measured, not assumed.

FIXED (branch feat/per-app-feature-flags):

  de93fa05c  /phoneme/languages  500 -> 200. supported_languages is a @property on
             UnifiedPhonemeEncoder returning a list, but the engine called it as a
             method: TypeError: 'list' object is not callable -> E_LANGUAGES_FAILED.
  de93fa05c  /phoneme/synthesize 500 -> 200. FOUND BY ME, not in the original 4: the
             voice engine returned a raw np.ndarray, which cannot cross JSON
             (E_SERIALIZATION). Now returns a WAV data-URI, matching the shape
             routers/multimodal.py already serves.
  6d11a88cf  /providers 500 -> 200. Split contract: the Provider protocol declares
             metadata a @property, but ct_provider / slonet_provider /
             slonet_server implement it as a plain METHOD, so the route put a bound
             method in the payload. App log names it exactly: "A method was returned
             instead of its value." Measured 31 ".metadata()" call sites vs 4
             property-style, so neither form works universally -> normalised at the
             read rather than churning 31 call sites across contended files.

TESTS: the reason all three survived is that the tests mocked what they asserted.
Every phoneme test injected _mock_engine(), and every /providers test registered NO
provider. Now 9/9 phoneme routes run against the real engine and /providers is
covered for BOTH metadata shapes. Negative control on each fix: reverting fails
exactly the new tests (rc=1), restoring gives 221 passed / 365 passed.

CORRECTION to this card's table for the last two rows — they answer, they are not
dead:

  /registry/artifacts  card says "200 in 11.8s". Measured 200 in 15.8s / 25.8s /
      33.6s / 46.4s — variable, load-dependent (box load average was 10-17).
      Same code in-process is 0.011-0.012s for the listing, so the handler is not
      the cost; the server scans 93 artifacts vs 26 in a bare process, and the box
      is loaded.

  /registry/verify  card says "no response in >15s / never answers, no status line".
      WRONG — it returns 504 Gateway Timeout at exactly 120.000s, logged as ERROR
      (log lines 07:40:55 and 07:43:16). It answers; the gateway times it out.

ROOT CAUSE for /registry/verify, and it is a design question not a bug: verify()
hashes EVERY artifact via streamed sha256, and the registry holds 3.99 GB — a
2,520,692,544-byte model.slnc plus a 988,097,824-byte model.safetensors among 93
items. A read-only GET that hashes 4 GB per call cannot land inside a 120s gateway
timeout on a thermally-clamped, load-17 laptop.

DECISION NEEDED before this row can be closed — pick one:
  (a) memoise hashes keyed on (path, size, mtime): same semantics, repeat calls fast,
      but the FIRST call still hashes 4 GB and can still miss the deadline;
  (b) default to a cheap size/mtime check with ?deep=1 for full hashing: changes what
      "verified" means, so it is a product call;
  (c) run the hash as a background job the route polls: new surface, needs the
      Endpoint & Transport Rule boundary discussion;
  (d) accept 504 and raise the gateway timeout: cheapest, hides the cost.

I recommend (b) with (a) underneath, but I am not taking that decision unilaterally
because it changes the meaning of the endpoint. Nothing in this card's remaining work
is a code defect — both rows are performance/design, not correctness.

LANDED on main 2026-10-12 (all CODE work complete; foreman session):
  e56d383fe /phoneme/languages  supported_languages is a @property -> drop parens. Real-engine seam test added. 19/19 pass.
  148782c30 /providers          default=str so one plugin's non-JSON metadata (datetime/engine handle) no longer 500s the whole listing.
  95dd65595 /providers          callable() normalization. slonet-native (SloNetChatProvider) + ct_provider + slonet_server expose metadata as a plain METHOD, so the property-style read put a bound method in the payload; default=str alone coerced it to the useless '<bound method ... at 0x...>' repr (200 with garbage). Both shapes now accepted. tests/server/test_inference_router.py 64 passed (TestProviders 3/3, registers one provider of each shape).
  e1ff46433 /phoneme/synthesize 5th dead route, ported from de93fa05c (feat/per-app-feature-flags, UNMERGED - that branch carries unrelated feature-flag work). Raw np.ndarray -> E_SERIALIZATION. Now a mono 22050 Hz WAV data-URI, same shape routers/multimodal.py serves. 19/19 pass.

COORD: the other session's STATUS above claims these fixed on feat/per-app-feature-flags (de93fa05c, 6d11a88cf). That branch is NOT merged; only the route fixes were ported. Its /providers fix (6d11a88cf, callable() normalization) is COMPLEMENTARY to the default=str one here - combined as 95dd65595.

REMAINING (NOT code): /registry/artifacts + /registry/verify are performance/design, per the a/b/c/d decision above. Surfaced to the user; no code defect open on this card.
title: Fix the 4 routes the site doctor found dead (2x500, 1 hang, 1 slow)

description:
Found by the site-doctor probe (`1c5abc300`, card e8fd60d4).
**(A) LANDED `99a16eae7`** on `fix/health-verdict-one-opinion`. **(B) still open.**

## (A) one verdict — DONE

`GET /health` answered `"healthy"` while `GET /health/detailed` answered
`"init"` for the same process. Two independent causes; fixing either alone
would have left the other to reintroduce it:

1. `get_basic_health` seeded `"status": "healthy"` as a **literal**, before any
   evaluation — the operator-facing endpoint was green on a server that had
   never reported itself running.
2. `/health/detailed` put the raw lifecycle **phase** into `status`, a field
   the rest of the system reads as a **verdict**: `health_flow` scores into
   exactly `{healthy, degraded, unhealthy}` and `test_health_router` already
   asserted that vocabulary. Detailed was answering a phase question with an
   unparseable value.

Both now call one function, `_derive_verdict(lifecycle, health_score)` —
**agreement by construction**, not two implementations that happen to match.

### Why the weighting makes a lifecycle gate necessary

`health_flow` already combines errors, latency, throughput, uptime and
resources into a composite score with per-check `OK/WARN/CRITICAL` severity.
On a freshly booted server it scored **92/"healthy" for a process still parked
in `init`** — because those counters are *absent rather than bad*. A score
that cannot see the lifecycle must not be the thing that declares health.

So: **lifecycle gates the verdict outright**; the weighted score only decides
once RUNNING is reached. `status` is a stable three-word verdict, the phase
stays in `lifecycle.phase`, and basic `/health` now carries `health_score`
with its diagnoses — because a verdict an agent cannot interrogate can only be
alerted on, not acted on. `_get_basic_health_score` defaults to `degraded`,
never healthy: failing open is the same defect this removes.

**Agent-layer framing:** this is the substrate — one document that answers
"are our checks ok" *and* shows its reasoning, for the underlying agent layer
that will later sit beneath infra and core with its own SlonET.

Gates: `test_health_router.py` (api-server) 22 + (core-py) 9 passed, ruff
clean. A/B proven — stashing the controller gives **5 failed, 17 passed**: all
17 pre-existing tests stay green on the broken code. Third consecutive defect
this session hidden behind tests asserting a shape rather than a meaning.

## (B) the orchestrator never calls `mgr.start()` — STILL OPEN

Verified chain, unchanged:

1. `StartupOrchestrator` registers **13 startup + 13 shutdown hooks** on the
   LifecycleManager, registers gates, calls `mgr.shutdown()` on exit
   (`infrastructure/startup.py:1189`) — but **never `mgr.start()`**.
2. `start()` is the only path to RUNNING (`lifecycle.py:595`), and
   `is_running()` is literally `phase == RUNNING`.
3. So the manager is parked at `INIT` forever; `phase` never leaves `init`.

**(A) does not fix (B)** — it only stops it being *hidden*. `/health` now
correctly reports `degraded` for a process that never started, which is
honest but still wrong-in-substance: the app *has* finished starting.

### Why (B) is not a one-line fix

`start()` runs all registered startup hooks, and the orchestrator has already
run those phases itself. A bare `await mgr.start()` would execute the 13 hooks
a **second** time. The real question is **who is the single startup driver** —
the orchestrator or the manager — which is architectural, not a patch.

Note `lifecycle.py` is pure asyncio (`asyncio.Lock/Event/gather`), while PGQ
(`pugqeep/`) is deliberately event-loop-free and already consumed by
`startup.py`/`main.py` (`Pool`, `Process`, `ProcessStatus`). Per the execution
philosophy the async host is a *consumer* of PGQ, so wiring the manager to PGQ
is legitimate — but it is a design choice to make explicitly.

### Adjacent work in flight — coordinate before touching (B)

- `.wt-gstage` `fix/gateway-health-startup-stage` — **5 uncommitted**
  (`apps/gateway/src/main.rs`, `apps/web/lib/health-blocks.ts` + tests)
- `.wt-gwstage` `feat/gateway-startup-stage` — **4 uncommitted**
  (`apps/gateway/src/main.rs`, `apps/web/hooks/useLiveStatus.ts`)

The Python files are free, but "startup stage" is the same concept — whoever
lands (B) must say which layer owns the phase.

## Scope note

The probe also reported `request_count=0` while `inference_count>0`. On a
fresh server both are 0 and `health_score` reads `healthy`/92. **Only the
`init`-vs-`healthy` contradiction was live**, and that half is fixed. The
metrics-unwired item should be re-checked after traffic, not assumed fixed.

**Acceptance for (B):** `phase` leaves `init` for a finished startup; re-run
`scripts/site_doctor_probe.py` — `lifecycle-stuck` must read `ok`.
title: Health surface contradicts itself: /health says healthy while /health/detailed says degraded

description:
FOUND 2026-10-12 while building the notes controller (card 10217777, landed 716c1c083). NOT FIXED here: store.py carries another session's uncommitted union-on-write change, so the file is off-limits.

WHAT: PlannerStore.delete_note(note_id) returns True, but the note is still readable afterwards.

ROOT CAUSE: _write_notes(notes) re-reads the journal and unions by id to protect against concurrent wipes — 'a record this snapshot never saw is kept verbatim'. A deliberate deletion is indistinguishable from a record the snapshot never saw, so the removed id is re-appended from disk on the very write that was meant to delete it. The write path has no way to express intent to remove.

PROBE:
    s = PlannerStore(board_dir=..., notes_dir=...)
    n = s.create_note('Delete me')
    s.delete_note(n.id)     -> True
    s.get_note(n.id)        -> Note('Delete me')   # survived

ALREADY FAILING AT BASELINE: packages/app-planner/tests/test_core.py::TestNoteStore::test_delete_note asserts exactly this (its fixture is a PlannerStore despite the class name). With or without the new controller tests: 263 passed / 1 failed. So the defect is live on the current tree, not introduced by 716c1c083.

FIX (suggested, for the owner of store.py): let _write_notes take an explicit removal set, e.g. _write_notes(notes, removed: set[str] | None = None), skip ids in  in both the caller loop and the disk-order union, and have delete_note pass {note_id}. Delete intent then wins over the union, while concurrent adds/edits keep being preserved. A tombstone record in the journal is the alternative but the journal is a plain note list, not an op log, so it costs more machinery for the same guarantee.

IMPACT IF IGNORED: every projection lies —  / the notes CLI print success and change nothing, so deleted notes silently come back on the next read and sync keeps re-creating their cards. A silent no-op is worse than an error: nothing fails, so nothing gets reported.

STOPGAP ALREADY IN PLACE: NotesController.delete() (716c1c083) verifies after the call — if the store reports success while the note is still readable it raises NoteStoreError instead of returning True. That stops the lie at the seam; it does not make deletion work. Its test asserts the invariant, not one branch, so it stays green both before and after the fix.
title: BUG: PlannerStore.delete_note returns True while the note survives (union-on-write re-appends deleted ids)

description:
Symptom: Quick test / chat assistant responses render with ALL spaces removed, e.g. 'lamavirtualassistantdesignedtoprovideinformationandanswerquestionsinvariousfields.Icangeneralinquiries,'. Punctuation survives (it rides inside the word token) but every inter-word space is gone. Truncation mid-word is the separate max_tokens=100 issue (fix C).

Ruled out (evidence):
- Frontend render: QuickActions.tsx renders {testResponse} as plain JSX text — React cannot strip spaces from a text node.
- Stream assembly: chat-controller.ts has no trim/replace on tokens; accumulated += token is faithful (only max_new_tokens ?? 100 at lines 47/66/95).
- No whitespace-removing regex anywhere on the py response path.

Root cause (decoder layer), domain/training/_internal/tokenizer.py — serving emits per-token decode (model_worker.py:432/718, model_server.py:315, numpy_engine.py:564, slonet_server.py:461):
1. SloBPE.decode (line 370): word separation depends entirely on _word_suffix matching vocab. gpt2 branch (402) STRIPS the marker; whitespace branch (405) converts it to a space. from_dict force-loads v1 files as 'whitespace' (439) and only persists the flag for version>=2 (424/436). A pretokenizer/vocab style mismatch therefore erases every word boundary.
2. Unigram decode (line 1291): bare raw = ''.join(tokens) with NO word-boundary restoration at all — if vocab entries are bare words, output is concatenated words by construction.
3. Single-token decode (408/1315) returns raw without strip, so whatever the prefix convention is, it is what the client concatenates.

Either path reproduces the observed output exactly. Fix candidate E, alongside A (frame/skip [CONSCIOUSNESS] block, managers.py:957), B (move engine.process() off the prompt-build read path, managers.py:912), C (raise max_tokens ?? 100, chat-controller.ts:47/66/95).

Next step: determine which tokenizer the loaded Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct serving path actually uses, then fix decode to be space-faithful under streaming (round-trip encode/decode test as the gate).
title: Quick test: decoder drops word boundaries (spaces stripped from streamed responses)

description:
FOUND 2026-10-12 while verifying card aab5df8b (which proved STALE — 476
passed on origin/main a01bc99b8). This is the residual that card's green
number hid.

WHAT
`domain/shell/_internal/repl.py:3379`, in `_cmd_chat_interactive`:

    user_input = input("  you> ")

It is the ONLY builtin `input()` in the file. Every other prompt reads through
the IO abstraction — `self.io.read(...)` at lines 480, 3991, 4192, 5238, 5251.

WHY IT MATTERS
`_run_with_io` and `_CaptureOutput` swap `repl.io` (and the console IOs) for a
MemoryIO so scripted runs are hermetic. builtin `input()` reads `sys.stdin`
directly and never sees that swap. Two consequences:

 1. Any captured / non-tty run raises OSError from stdin. The inner handler
    catches only (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt) and the outer only
    KeyboardInterrupt — so OSError propagates out of `_cmd_chat_interactive`
    uncaught.
 2. Interactive chat is the one mode where a real user's keystrokes bypass the
    abstraction the rest of the shell is built on.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT
origin/main's `TestCmdChat::test_chat_no_args` asserts `_last_exit_code == 1`
with the comment "the fixture mocks [the API] down, so the gate refuses
first." The gate refuses, interactive mode is never entered, and line 3379 is
never reached. The tests are green because they do not exercise the code.

THE FIX (1 line)
    user_input = self.io.read("  you> ")
`MemoryIO` raises EOFError once its queue is exhausted, which is exactly the
path already treated as "leave chat". No existing test changes.

ALREADY EXISTS ELSEWHERE — PORT, DO NOT REBUILD
`d3c20f708` on branch `fix/journal-append-race` made this same one-line change
plus rewrote ~10 tests. The code half is what we need. Its test half is NOT
ported: it rewrote tests asserting `exit_code == 1` to assert `0`, which would
change what the gate tests mean. We add one new test instead and leave the
existing suite untouched.

A/B REQUIRED: stashing the 1-line fix must make the new test fail.

PROBE (with the gate stubbed to pass, driven through the IO abstraction):

    with patch.object(repl, "_require_api", return_value=True):
        _run_with_io(repl, [], lambda: repl._cmd_chat(""))
    assert repl._last_exit_code == 0

    broken -> OSError: pytest: reading from stdin while output is captured!
    fixed  -> EOFError -> "[exiting chat]" -> exit 0
title: shell chat interactive loop bypasses the IO abstraction — latent OSError, untested on main
