description:
User directive: "chars should be on the tree and called core tokenizer format native — to know what we have"; build it BACKWARD COMPATIBLE (user overrode the risk-based deferral: "build it so its backward compatible").

PROBLEM: native models tokenize through two ad-hoc wrappers in domain/inference/_internal/slonet_provider.py (_CharTokenizer stoi/itos, _TreeTokenizer TokenTree) with no format identity — nothing on the object or the .soul says which format it is, so "which tokenizer served this?" needs a code crawl (the a4705a55 lesson). Vocab for char models lives OUTSIDE the tree machinery.

DESIGN (data unification, semantics stay per-format):
1. NativeTokenizer — one wrapper; ALWAYS carries a TokenTree (char: tree.vocab/stoi/itos built from the checkpoint stoi/itos — chars literally ON the tree; empty trie, _trained=False). encode/decode dispatch on scheme:
   - native/token-tree: exact current _TreeTokenizer behavior (tree.encode/decode incl. lowercase normalize + pretokenize).
   - native/char: exact current _CharTokenizer behavior (raw per-char, NO normalize, OOV->0, decode raw join, eos=stoi.get(chr(10),0), pad=0, vocab_size=max_key+1).
   Backward-compat contract: bit-identical encode/decode/eos/pad/vocab_size on legacy fixtures for BOTH formats; _CharTokenizer/_TreeTokenizer names stay importable (tests/core-py/test_slonet_provider.py + test_slonet_kv_benchmark.py import them); apply_chat_template hoisted (identical duplicate today).
2. Format tag on save: top-level soul.metadata["tokenizer_format"] = "native/char" | "native/token-tree" (parallel key — existing readers of metadata["stoi"]/metadata["tokenizer"] untouched). Load: ONE from_metadata helper at both load sites (from_soul + embedded-emb loader); tag read if present, else DERIVED FROM CONTENT (tree present -> token-tree, stoi/itos -> char); CONTENT WINS on disagreement (it is what encode/decode will actually use) + warning log.
3. origin: checkpoint path threaded where naturally in hand (from_slnc(path)), optional=None elsewhere; field only, NO log lines / NO API surfacing (user answered surface: off).

FILE SAFETY: domain/training/_internal/tokenizer.py is DIRTY with another session WIP — NOT touched (SloBPE/SloUnigram provenance deferred). Targets: slonet_provider.py, train_pipeline.py (save stamp — verified clean), tests.

GATES: new tests/core-py/test_native_tokenizer_format.py (legacy bit-identity x2, tag round-trip, content-wins-on-mismatch, old names importable, apply_chat_template parity); existing test_slonet_provider.py, test_slonet_kv_benchmark.py, token_tree suites; ruff check+format.
title: Native core tokenizer format: chars on the tree, one scheme/origin surface (backward compatible)

description:
Landed on branch fix/a4705a55-decode-spaces, sha 28e496fd4 (worktree .wt-decodespace), based on main a07a4525e.

Card moved done -> review: at the time it read done there was NO landed sha on main — done needs evidence.

Diff: domain/training/_internal/tokenizer.py + packages/core-py/tests/test_tokenizer.py only (git show --stat 28e496fd4 = 2 files, +155/-4). Four round-trip tests written first and shown red (3 failed, 1 passed) before the fix.

Root cause (supersedes the card's SloBPE/Unigram guess): the Qwen serving path instantiates MorphTokenizer, which round-trips correctly; the reachable-broken paths are SloBPE/SloUnigram via the shared-manager fallback. encode() marks every pretoken end with </w> and degrades unrepresentable chars to <UNK>; on a byte-level (G-hat) vocab — which has neither a literal space nor a </w> token — the inter-word space AND the marker both become <UNK>, so decode(skip_special=True) drops them as structural specials while raw.replace(_word_suffix, ...) is a no-op. Fix: a vocab is byte-level iff it carries G-hat and no </w>; encode then emits the leading space as its own token, decode maps it back before the single-token fast path (streaming stays lossless). </w> vocabs keep the original path, guarded by a test.

Foreman verification: 4 tokenizer files exit=0, 0 FAILED (168 tests); ruff check + format clean on both files; merge-tree dry run main...branch rc=0.

NOT MERGED: same quiet-window reason as the health card.

description:
## What

One shared SSE keepalive primitive, lifted from the one place it worked.

Measured surface: **59 StreamingResponse sites across 16 routers**. Heartbeats
hand-rolled in 4 routers under **3 different variable names**
(`_last_heartbeat` x9, `_last_yield` x6, `last_heartbeat` x3). **9 routers /
26 sites have no keepalive at all** (chat, session, tools, mobile, souls,
agents, models, shell, system). The working implementation lived in
`apps/api/server/training/sse_stream.py` and was coupled to
`build_training_sse_response`, so only 2 consumers could reach it.

## Landed

`01344c443` on `feat/sse-keepalive-primitive` (off origin/main `a01bc99b8`).

- `domain/api/_internal/sse_envelope.py` — `StreamPacing`,
  `SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL` (10.0), `SSE_HEARTBEAT_FRAME`. Placed here, not in a
  new module: `domain.api` already owns the SSE envelope, so every consumer
  already importing it gets liveness for free.
- `apps/api/server/infrastructure/sse_fallback.py` — re-exports all three with
  a pure-Python fallback, so routers keep one import path.
- `apps/api/server/training/sse_stream.py` — drops its hand-rolled copy.
  10 insertions / 10 deletions, **no signature change**.

## The design constraint worth keeping

A `with_keepalive(async_generator)` adapter cannot work, and the failure is
invisible on the wire. `asyncio.wait_for` CANCELS its awaitable on timeout, and
cancelling `anext()` throws into the generator at its await point. Measured on
CPython 3.12.14:

    silence 1 -> TimeoutError   (frame already cancelled)
    silence 2 -> StopAsyncIteration (frame gone)

So the adapter emits exactly one heartbeat and then **closes the stream** — and
a clean close reads as normal end-of-stream, so the client sees success while
the route still looks healthy for having sent bytes. That is the worst available
failure mode. The timing must therefore live on the consumer's side of the
yield, where the coroutine being abandoned is a plain `queue.get()`.

Hence: extract the *invariant* (cadence, exact bytes, deadline arithmetic) and
leave the loop with the consumer.

## Gates

- `tests/contract/test_sse_keepalive.py` — **7 passed** (new). Includes the
  adapter-failure pin above so the code comment cannot drift from what the
  interpreter actually does, and a functional test proving the queue pattern
  survives repeated silence and still delivers a real event.
- `tests/contract` 21 passed; `tests/server/test_startup_routers.py` 49 passed;
  `tests/test_layer_conformance.py` 3 passed.
- Training suites (runtime / router_kwds / status_transitions /
  audit_instrumentation / webhook_consolidation / schemas) — **100 passed**.
- `ruff check` clean on all 5 files.

## Assumptions

- **API routers only.** The Rust gateway's SSE/compression path and the web
  client's reconnect behaviour are out of scope — separate toolchain, separate
  card.
- **10s cadence.** Training already streamed at 10s; unification adopts the
  plurality. The 30s `/errors/stream` cadence is not migrated here.

## Follow-ups (NOT in this change)

1. Migrate the 4 hand-rolled sites (`consciousness.py`, `errors.py`,
   `infer.py`, `inference.py`) to `StreamPacing`.
2. Add keepalives to the 26 bare sites — `chat.py` and `session.py` first;
   those are the streams a user actually sits on.
3. Derive the site-doctor probe's `STREAM_GRACE` from `SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL`
   instead of parsing cadences out of router source. **Blocked**: the probe
   (`scripts/site_doctor_probe.py`) is not in origin/main yet — it is on
   `feat/site-doctor-sse-triage` in the pending cherry-pick queue.

## Status

Implemented and green. **Merge is not approved by this card** — it joins the
pending cherry-pick series awaiting an explicit call.
title: SSE keepalive: one shared primitive in domain.api

description:
## Why this card exists (it corrects card d14cee64)

d14cee64 shipped the shared keepalive primitive (`StreamPacing`) and listed
"add keepalives to the 27 bare sites — health.py and dashboard.py first" as
follow-up 2. **That priority was wrong.** Inspecting the bare sites:

| site | shape | can it sit silent? | does a keepalive help? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `health.startup_stream` | fixed 1.0s cadence, terminates at ready | no | **no** — always emits |
| `health.health_stream` | fixed 3.0s cadence, body in `to_thread` | only when the build hangs | **no in-loop** |
| `dashboard.generate` | fixed cadence, body in `to_thread` | only when the build hangs | **no in-loop** |
| `system.generate` | `sub.async_read(timeout=0.2)` | **yes** | **yes** |
| `tools.unknown_stream` | one-shot error frame | no | no |
| `tools.generate` | token stream awaiting inference | maybe | not this card |

These routers are bare **because the loop is the clock**. An interleaved
keepalive cannot fire while the loop is blocked — so on `health_stream` it
would be dead code that never executes. The training loop is different: it
reads from a queue fed by an external producer, so silence is genuinely
possible and the keepalive means something.

## The actual defect on the health surface

`health.py:812`

    snapshot = await asyncio.to_thread(self._build_health_snapshot, ctrl)

`_build_health_snapshot` → `ctrl.get_detailed_health()` is synchronous and
**unbounded**, called with no timeout. If any subsystem check blocks — a lock,
a subprocess, a network call — the stream stalls *forever* and emits nothing.

A stalled health stream is the worst possible failure on this surface: it is
indistinguishable from a healthy one to any observer, and it is precisely the
surface goal (A) requires an underlying agent layer to read. Silence must mean
"nothing to report", never "I am wedged".

## Scope

1. **`routers/health.py` — make a stall visible, and bound it.**
   - Run the snapshot build as a single long-lived `asyncio.Task`, polled with
     `wait_for(shield(task))`. `shield` is load-bearing: cancelling a bare
     `wait_for(to_thread(...))` abandons the future but the thread keeps
     running, so a naive retry-every-cycle would spawn a new thread pool thread
     every 3s while the check is wedged. Shielded, exactly **one** build is
     ever in flight and the generator just polls it.
   - After `HEALTH_SNAPSHOT_STALL_S` (= 3x the cadence) with no fresh
     snapshot, emit a stall event carrying elapsed time, then keep the loop
     alive — the stream must not die, and must not raise a false alarm for a
     snapshot that is merely slower than its cadence.
2. **`routers/system.py` — the genuine keepalive gap.** `sub.async_read`
   returns within 0.2s even when the subprocess is silent, so the loop reaches
   the top every 0.2s and a `StreamPacing` check actually gets a chance to
   fire. Adopts the shared primitive — the **second, unrelated consumer**,
   which is the real test of whether d14cee64 extracted a primitive or merely
   moved a helper.

**Explicitly deferred** (recorded, not forgotten): `dashboard.py` is the same
defect as health and takes the same fix mechanically once this pattern is
proven; `tools.generate` needs a separate judgement about bounding the
inference await.

## Gates

- ruff on touched files
- new contract tests: the stall event fires only past the threshold; exactly
  one build task exists while a check is wedged (no thread accumulation); the
  stream survives a stall and recovers; the keepalive fires on `system` under
  silence
- existing health/system router tests stay green

## Status

todo — brief written, not yet started.
title: Diagnostic streams: surface a stalled health check, keepalive on system

description:
Goal: run the curses shell TUI in the web UI, like opencode web.

Context established by measurement (not assumption):
- Three terminal surfaces exist; none can render a curses TUI.
  * TerminalPanel  -> POST /shell/exec (req/resp), returns a PROCESSED string;
                      apps/web/lib/ansi.ts is an SGR style parser, explicitly
                      NOT an emulator ("a full VT100 emulator would be dead
                      weight here"), drops all cursor motion.
  * V86TerminalPanel -> SSE, sanitizeVmOutput handles only ESC[2J + \b and
                      strips every other sequence (broken for full-screen apps).
  * curses TUI      -> emits real cursor motion + alt screen (ESC[?1049h via
                      graphics.py, curses windows in tui_repl._render_all);
                      unreachable from the browser.
- No xterm.js dependency anywhere (apps/web/package.json has no terminal dep).
- Precedent for WS already in-repo: inference.py:1489 ws_generate
  (accept -> auth -> receive_text/send_json).
- Reference decoder already written and tested: tests/core-py/test_shell_tui_live.py
  decodes the pty byte stream into a persistent 80x24 frame.

Design (expert-reviewed, approved):
Alt-screen and scrollback are two BUFFERS OF ONE VT100 STATE MACHINE, not two
models. Build one engine, two projections:

  pty (server) --WS raw bytes--> SHELL ENGINE (client, primary+scrollback |
                                  alternate buffer)
                                      |-- projection A: alt frame -> <TermScreen> (TUI)
                                      |-- projection B: line log  -> <TerminalPanel>

PHASE 1 SCOPE (this card):
1. WS /shell/term carrying raw framed pty bytes + {resize rows,cols}, modelled
   on the existing ws_generate auth pattern.
2. From-scratch VT100 emulator, scoped to the sequence families the TUI
   actually emits (cursor addressing, alt screen, SGR, erase). Allowlist of
   sequence families -- deliberately NOT "interpret everything".
3. New <TermScreen> component rendering the ALTERNATE buffer.
4. Validate the emulator against the existing 80x24 decoder as reference.

ROOT CAUSE, fully characterized (read-only; supersedes an earlier card that misfiled this as a live bug):

The 788 'journal: chain broken' findings are HISTORICAL RESIDUE, not a live defect. The append race that caused them was already found and fixed by 8ca177458 (2026-10-10 06:35, 'close the slot_history append race', card d708578d), which added append_lines_checked: one flock, size revalidated with the lock held, rebase() rebuilding the payload from a fresh tail read.

Evidence the fix holds:
- Last fork stamped 2026-10-10T01:20:07, five hours BEFORE the fix landed.
- Zero forks across the 32 board commits since (through 2026-10-13).
- 0 rehash mismatches, 0 gaps, 0 first-node faults across 92,156 nodes / 1,228 slots. Every one of the 788 breaks is a true fork, and 788/788 (100%) link to the GRANDPARENT, produced by only 12 distinct timestamps (6 bulk events, ~130-150 nodes each). That 100% uniformity is the signature of a deterministic stale-snapshot batch write, not interleaved concurrency.

THE ACTUAL REMAINING PROBLEM: verify_board reports 788 findings against healthy production data. A gate that always screams is a disabled gate — a NEW fork would be finding #789 and nobody would see it. Same failure mode as any unbaselined ratchet.

ASK: make the gate actionable without losing forensics. Suggested shape — time is the honest discriminator, since the fix boundary is precisely known: forks stamped at or before the fix are reported only under an opt-in include_historical flag (default off, so the gate is quiet and usable); any fork stamped after it is a live regression and must fail loudly. Full forensic detail stays one flag away.

DO NOT rewrite the journal to 'repair' the 788 forks without explicit user approval. It is append-only by design, and current board STATE is already correct — load_journal takes the last node per slot as the tip, so the forks are superseded mid-chain history, not corrupted current state. Repairing buys cosmetics at the cost of the append-only property.
title: verify_board returns 788 findings on a HEALTHY board — historical forks drown the gate (ratchet pre-fix residue)

description:
WHAT: Unify the native tokenizer so char and token-tree are ONE algorithm, not two branches.
  User: "characters makes up tokens... we dont need separate char and token in native tokenizer implementation."

FINDING: TokenTree.query() does greedy longest-prefix match; over a depth-1 trie that
  reduces to exactly stoi.get(c,0) = the legacy _CharTokenizer body. One algorithm, two
  configs. NativeTokenizer.encode branches on self.variant -> two drifted code paths.

FIVE policy knobs must be hoisted (not one): pretokenizer none|gpt2, lowercase F|T,
  word_suffix ""|</w>, oov_id 0|unk_id, decode raw-join|skip-specials+spaces.
  TRAP: naive degenerate tree returns unk_id(1) on OOV; legacy char returns 0.
  test_oov_char_maps_to_zero pins encode("z")==[0]. Skip this and every existing
  char-vocab model silently changes ids (same silent-corruption class as SessionKVCache).

LANDMINE: query() does `if ch == "<": ... break` for multi-piece specials and never falls
  through to single-char lookup. Real tree unaffected; char vocab containing "<" would
  start returning OOV. Fix: fall through to node.children.get(ch).

PLAN: (1) TokenTree policy object (pretokenizer/lowercase/word_suffix/oov_id/
  skip_special_decode). (2) query uses self._oov_id + falls through on unmatched "<".
  (3) encode honours policy. (4) decode honours policy. (5) NativeTokenizer DELETES the
  variant branch; variant stays a provenance LABEL only (test asserts variant=="char" and
  pretokenizer is None). (6) _char_carrier_tree builds a REAL depth-1 trie via _add_token.
  (7) to_dict/from_dict round-trip policy with defaults so legacy .soul loads identically.

GATE: tests/core-py/test_native_tokenizer_format.py (278 lines) asserts byte-identity vs
  INDEPENDENT inline oracles (_legacy_char_encode/_legacy_char_decode frozen in test body).
  test_oov_char_maps_to_zero, test_case_is_preserved, test_decode_arbitrary_ids_byte_identical.
  Behaviour-preserving => they pass; not => they fail loudly. Do NOT weaken them.

BENCH: re-run battery as THREE rows (char folds into tree). Prior: Morph 11/11 F1 @1619 rt/s,
  SloBPE 3/11 @157k, SloUnigram 4/11 @214k, char 4/11 @3.63M, tree 3/11 @610k.
  F1/F2 shortfalls were OOV coverage, NOT decode bugs (verified) - judge on parity-green
  + char throughput vs 3.6M, not raw F1.

FOLLOW-ON (separate commit): SloUnigram._all_segmentations enumerates every segmentation
  into a list - exponential in pretoken length; one 48-char unbroken word hangs/OOMs train().

SHARED: index updated n/a (no new doc/module) | shared copy reused yes (one TokenTree, no
  dep) | coordination named - gate file tests/core-py/test_native_tokenizer_format.py;
  slonet_provider.py + token_tree.py were CLEAN at pickup 2026-10-13.
title: Native tokenizer: unify char + token-tree into ONE algorithm (policy hoisted)

That was inflated: it matched store METHOD calls such as get().fetch() in apps/web/lib/operations-store.ts (4 hits, that file already uses apiGet/apiPost from http-client) and packages/sdk-ts client.ts's own private request() body. Using a lookbehind that excludes member access ((?<![\w.$])fetch\s*\() the true count is 40: apps/web 19, apps/mobile 17, packages/sdk-ts 4.

ALL THREE FRONTENDS ALREADY HAVE A REQUEST LAYER.
The card assumes they do not and must be given one. They do:

  packages/sdk-ts .../src/client.ts   private request<T>()
A filename search for 'http-client.ts' alone is what produced the earlier wrong belief that mobile and sdk-ts had no client layer. Only web uses that filename.

MOST OF THE 40 SITES ARE DELIBERATE, NOT BYPASSES.

                      Anthropic /messages, Gemini :streamGenerateContent?key= — per-vendor baseUrl,
                      apiKey and wire protocol. api-client.ts resolves OUR server (getApiUrl() ->

The three sdk-ts streaming endpoints (chatStream/generateStream/regenerateStream) talked to OUR
server, hand-rolled fetch, and passed NO AbortSignal — so a connection accepted but never answered
hung the caller forever. Extracted fetchResponse() owning timeout + ok-check + AbortError->408;
client.ts went 4 raw fetch( to 1. RED->GREEN (3 failed/228 skipped -> all pass); 231 passed,
tsc exit 0, eslint 0 errors. Timeout clears on header arrival, deliberately, so long generations
are not aborted mid-stream.

lack timeout discipline.' The blanket version would break streaming and misroute external traffic.

description:
WHAT: SloUnigram.train hangs/OOMs on any long unbroken word. Discovered while
  re-running the tokenizer battery for card 8fefc101.

ROOT CAUSE: `_all_segmentations` in domain/training/_internal/tokenizer.py
  materializes EVERY segmentation of a pretoken into a list. That is exponential
  in pretoken length. A single 48-char word
  ("lamavirtualassistantdesignedtoprovideinformation") is enough to hang or OOM
  train(). A 9-line corpus containing just one such word never finishes.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is not an exotic input. URLs, base64 blobs, identifiers,
  camelCase compounds and file paths are all unbroken runs. Any real corpus hits
  it, so SloUnigram is effectively untrainable outside toy data — which is why
  the battery needs a per-phase alarm to complete at all.

FIX DIRECTION: do not enumerate. Score segmentations lazily (generator /
  beam / DP over the lattice) and keep only the k best. The memory that matters
  is the frontier, not the full cartesian product.

GATE: a 48-char unbroken word must train within a bounded time. The battery
  (scripts/benchmark_tokenizer_battery.py) already carries that word as its last
  case — make it a hard assertion once fixed, and drop the 60s alarm for this.

EVIDENCE: found in battery runs for 8fefc101 (commit 2bfabac5f).
title: SloUnigram.train hangs: _all_segmentations enumerates every segmentation (exponential in pretoken length)

description:
WHAT: TokenTree.train raises ValueError for vocab_size >= 256 on small corpora:
  "Accuracy must be 0-1, got -0.1719..." (value varies run to run).

ROOT CAUSE: TokenTree.train builds embedding Points and hands them to pugqeep's
  PointLibrary.add, which validates `0.0 <= point.accuracy <= 1.0`
  (packages/core-py/domains/infrastructure/pugqeep/library.py:419). The point
  comes from PointCompressor.compress_cluster (k-means/Lloyd refit), which can
  emit an accuracy outside [0,1]. More vocab -> more points -> higher chance one
  is out of range.

EVIDENCE THAT IT IS PRE-EXISTING (verified, not introduced by 8fefc101):
  - pristine HEAD fails identically at vocab_size=256 (checked by restoring the
    original files and re-running);
  - in-process TokenTree.train is deterministic (two runs give identical vocab
    and merges), so the cross-process variance is the k-means RNG, not hashing —
    PYTHONHASHSEED=0 does NOT stabilize it;
  - only vocab_size >= 256 fails; 128 succeeds.

IMPACT: blocks training any tree larger than ~128 tokens on a small corpus, and
  makes results irreproducible across runs (a benchmark hazard).

FIX DIRECTION: (1) clamp/validate accuracy at the compressor boundary rather
  than letting PointLibrary reject it, and (2) seed the k-means RNG so embedding
  Points are reproducible.

GATE: TokenTree().train(corpus, vocab_size=512) succeeds; two runs produce
  byte-identical to_dict().

WORKAROUND IN PLACE: scripts/benchmark_tokenizer_battery.py uses vocab_size=128
  and documents why in a comment. Lift that once fixed.
title: TokenTree.train fails at vocab>=256: pugqeep compress_cluster emits accuracy outside [0,1], and k-means RNG makes runs irreproducible

description:
WHAT: Put SloBPE into the core native tokenizer format as a lossless conversion
  — user: "put them in core tokenizer" / "then see how they compare as a whole
  [with] native tokenizer we just added as token tree and char".

PRECONDITION PROVEN (this is what makes the conversion safe):
  SloBPE.train and TokenTree.train are the same algorithm AND produce the SAME
  OUTPUT. Matched parameters (lowercase=X for both):
    lowercase=False -> 81 merges each, 81 shared, 0 bpe-only, 0 tree-only, vocab IDENTICAL
    lowercase=True  -> 82 merges each, 82 shared, 0 bpe-only, 0 tree-only, vocab IDENTICAL
  An earlier probe claimed "9/10 disagree, 71 shared, 81 vs 82 merges" — that was
  a PROBE BUG (SloBPE trained lowercase=False, TokenTree defaulted to True).
  Corrected: identical vocab + 100% shared merges.

  The residual 2/10 encode disagreement is NOT vocab — it is SloBPE.encode
  calling _normalize on input (.strip() + re.sub(r"\s+"," ",..)) which destroys
  data Tree preserves:
    '  leading and trailing  '  bpe -> 'leading and trailing'   tree -> preserved
    'line one\nline two\n'      bpe -> 'line one line two'      (newlines collapsed)
  Converting BPE into core therefore also RETIRES the lossy round-trip.

SCOPE:
  + NativeTokenizer.from_slo_bpe() — build the trie + lineage from SloBPE's
    vocab/merges (TokenTree.from_dict needs a trie; SloBPE.to_dict has none),
    wrap as NativeTokenizer(variant="tree").
  + battery row proving core-BPE == tree through the same interface.

OUT OF SCOPE (recorded, not silently dropped):
  - SloUnigram CANNOT convert: it is a Viterbi lattice walk, not a greedy trie
    walk. Forcing it in would re-fork encode/decode — the exact branch the
    char/tree unification removed. Stays its own scheme "training/unigram".
  - lowercase persistence: train(lowercase=False) never writes self._lowercase,
    and SloBPE/SloUnigram encode hardcode literal True (lines 279/1176/1213).
    Real incoherence BUT lowercasing-at-encode is PINNED CONTRACT
      test_lowercase_normalization_active: tree MUST lowercase
      test_case_is_preserved: char must NOT
    and it provably moves NO battery score (corpus has no uppercase). Follow-on.

CONTRACTS THAT MUST NOT BREAK:
  test_one_scheme_per_family_and_uniform_attrs (card 85dedb7e) — schemes stay
  {"native","hf","training/bpe","training/unigram"}; BPE does not become "native".
  test_delegates_encode_decode_to_tree / test_chars_live_on_the_tree — NativeTokenizer
  stays a TokenTree wrapper; no duck-typed dispatch.
  test_native_tokenizer_format.py 37 byte-parity tests.

  shared copy reused — yes, no new module/dependency; converts into existing TokenTree.
  coordination named — token_tree.py / slonet_provider.py owned by card 8fefc101
    (branch feat/tokenspace-char-tree-unify, sha 2bfabac5f, status review).

description:
WHAT: The `lowercase` training argument does not reach encode, in three places
  two different ways. A model trained with lowercase=False still folds case on
  encode, leaving uppercase vocabulary entries that are unreachable.

  TokenTree.train(lowercase=...) uses it ONLY for corpus prep. self._lowercase
    is assigned in __init__ (default True) and never again — grep
    "_lowercase *=" finds no assignment outside __init__.
    encode/decode read self._lowercase, so the constructor default wins.
    -> uppercase tokens land in the vocab (verified: ' CASE</w>', ' CAS') and
       encode("Hello World") still returns "hello world". Dead vocabulary.
  SloBPE.encode    passes the literal lowercase=True (tokenizer.py:279)
  SloUnigram.encode / encode_with_scores pass the literal (1176, 1213)

WHY NOT FIXED ALREADY (deliberately deferred):
  Lowercasing-at-encode is a PINNED FORMAT CONTRACT, not an accident:
    test_lowercase_normalization_active — native/token-tree MUST lowercase
      (tok.encode("THE CAT") == tok.encode("the cat"))
    test_case_is_preserved — native/char MUST NOT
    TestNormalize.test_no_lowercasing — _normalize itself honours the flag
  So the incoherence is narrow: only `train(lowercase=False)` failing to
  persist. And it provably moves NO battery score (verified by running the
  battery with build_tree at lowercase=False — identical F1/F2), because
  CORPUS has just one uppercase char.

PROPOSED FIX (needs a call, because it changes a contract):
  Persist: TokenTree.train writes self._lowercase; SloBPE/SloUnigram gain a
  _lowercase field set by train, read by encode instead of the literal.
  Default stays True, so every default path and the format contract above
  are unaffected; only an explicit lowercase=False caller changes behaviour.
  DECISION NEEDED: should native/token-tree be allowed to opt OUT of
  lowercasing at all, given it is documented as part of the format? If the
  answer is no, the correct fix is the opposite — remove/deprecate the
  lowercase=False path from train instead of honouring it.

GATE: whatever is chosen, test_lowercase_normalization_active and
  test_case_is_preserved are the acceptance tests. Do not weaken either.
  Also re-run scripts/benchmark_tokenizer_battery.py (a case-faithful tree row
  would be a NEW row, not a replacement — char already covers that role).

FILES: domain/training/_internal/token_tree.py (train),
  domain/training/_internal/tokenizer.py (SloBPE.encode 279, SloUnigram 1176/1213).

SHARED WORKSPACE: no new module, no index change. Coordination: token_tree.py
  is owned by card 8fefc101 (review) and touched by d0d36f55 (review).
title: tokenizer: train(lowercase=False) never reaches encode — 3 sites, 2 ways; contract-bound

description:
The parity gate (scripts/check_docs_api_parity.py) reports 'routers w/o tests: 2 [model_stack, phoneme]' on main. Probing those two routers found that the missing coverage is hiding real defects, not merely absent assertions.

BUG 1 — GET /phoneme/languages -> 500.
domain/voice/_internal/phoneme.py:178 does 'langs = encoder.supported_languages()'. The encoder is UnifiedPhonemeEncoder (line 47-49) and supported_languages is a LIST ATTRIBUTE, not a method — packages/core-py/tests/test_unified_phoneme_encoder.py:254-261 asserts '"en" in enc.supported_languages"'. Calling it raises 'list' object is not callable, which line 180 catches and turns into PhonemeResult(success=False), which the router converts to HTTP 500 E_LANGUAGES_FAILED. Observed live: 'ERR phoneme Supported languages failed: list object is not callable'. Fix is to drop the call parens.

BUG 2 — POST /model-stack/push with a missing 'name' -> 404.
apps/api/server/routers/model_stack.py:80 does 'name = payload["name"]' on an untyped dict, so a KeyError reaches classify_and_raise and is reported as HTTP 404 E_NOT_FOUND ['name']. A missing required body field is a validation failure (422), not a missing resource — the client is told the URL does not exist when the request body was malformed. Verified live: push {"path": "/tmp/x"} -> 404 'Resource not found.'

WHY THIS MATTERS: both are the exact failure mode that absent coverage permits. Neither router has a single test, and both are broken in ways a single happy-path assertion would have caught.

SCOPE: add router-level tests for all 14 routes (model-stack 5, phoneme 9) under apps/api/server/tests (the dirs the gate actually scans — note TEST_DIRS is (tests/server, apps/api/server/tests) and deliberately excludes packages/core-py/tests, which is why the phoneme encoder tests do not count as router coverage). Fix both defects. Drive the gate finding from 2 -> 0.

GATES: parity gate 'routers w/o tests' 2 -> 0; new tests RED before fix, GREEN after; no regressions in the server test dir; branch merges clean to origin/main.
title: Two untested routers hide two live defects: GET /phoneme/languages 500s ('list' object is not callable), POST /model-stack/push returns 404 for a missing field

description:
MEASURED (2026-10-14, battery session): laptop pulling 21-35W on battery with the dev stack idle-ish; GPU at 0%, governor powersave already. CPU-side steady-state wakers found in the server:

1. gateway bandwidth mirror polls http://127.0.0.1:8080/health/detailed every POLL_INTERVAL_S=5.0s FOREVER (domain/infrastructure/_internal/gateway_bandwidth.py:50, _loop:219-222). The Rust gateway is DEAD INFRA (card ux-012c-gateway-rollback) - on this deployment every poll is a guaranteed connection-refused: 720 wasted wakeups/hour, thread never sleeps deeper than 5s.

2. engine watcher busy-polls Popen.poll() + time.sleep(10) (apps/api/server/infrastructure/startup.py:1980-1986). A blocking proc.wait() detects exit instantly with ZERO wakeups (10s poll loop also delays crash detection up to 10s).

FIX: (1) exponential backoff on consecutive poll failures - base 5s, cap 60s (POLL_INTERVAL_MAX_S), reset to base on success; connected+active stays at 5s so the monitoring UI cadence is untouched; MAN_GATEWAY_URL="" still disables entirely. Tradeoff: gateway cold-start discovery takes up to 60s - acceptable for a metrics mirror, documented in the docstring. (2) _start_engine_watcher: proc.wait() on the daemon thread; returns the thread for testability.

Gates: tests/core-py/test_gateway_bandwidth.py (extend: backoff progression, cap, reset-on-success, idle-connected stays fast) + new watcher test + ruff. Landing rides the main-tree lane quiet window (main tree holds another session branch + heavy WIP).

description:
Originally quick-test fix C (three lines). Investigation widened it: same defect shape as card 66bf07ef (ModelStack) - a value ADVERTISED to the user and read by nothing.

EVIDENCE.
(1) apps/web/lib/chat-controller.ts:47 POSTs /chat with `max_tokens: options?.max_tokens ?? 100`; :66 fallback /inference/generate `max_new_tokens ?? 100`; :95 /chat/stream `max_new_tokens ?? 100`. No production caller passes max_tokens, so EVERY message is capped at 100 - that is the truncation users see.
(2) apps/api/server/schemas/config.py:15 GenerationConfig.max_new_tokens: int = Field(default=300, ge=1, le=4096) is user-configurable - the frontend exposes it at lib/settings-controller.ts:8 and lib/generation-config-controller.ts:5 - but grep across apps/api/server and domain finds ZERO consumers of gen_config.max_new_tokens. The only _gen_config reads are max_context_length (inference.py:2478/2488/2994) and gen_config.temperature (config.py:10). THE SETTINGS CONTROL DOES NOTHING FOR CHAT.
(3) inference.py:259 ChatRequest.max_tokens default is 128, so the frontend 100 also undercuts the schema default.
(4) TRAP: inference.py:162-190 _trim_messages_to_budget computes budget = max_context - max_new_tokens and at :177 returns ONLY system messages when remaining <= 0. max_context_length defaults to 1024; domain/training/_internal/auto_config.py:69 trains at max_seq_length 512. A naive frontend bump to 512 on a 512-context model would WIPE conversation history - trading reply truncation for total amnesia, strictly worse. The budget cannot be chosen in the frontend: only the backend knows max_context_length.

DECISION. Single authority, resolved at request time on the backend: effective = req.max_tokens when explicitly supplied, else min(_gen_config.max_new_tokens, _gen_config.max_context_length // 2). The clamp only bites when the configured budget would eat the context - exactly when it must. Frontend omits max_tokens unless the caller supplied it (pattern already used by lib/tools-controller.ts:85), so the configured value flows through.

WHY NOT SIMPLY BUMP 100 -> 300 IN THE FRONTEND: it would still ignore user config (setting 1024 gets overridden), duplicate a number that already lives in the schema, and leave the dead Settings control dead - three defects papered over instead of one fixed.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: flat raise of ChatRequest.max_tokens 128 -> 512, unsafe on small-context models per (4).

NOTE: the model validator at inference.py:286-288 resolves the max_new_tokens alias by testing `self.max_tokens == 128`. Making max_tokens None-by-default requires rewriting that branch to fire when max_tokens is None, else the alias silently dies.
title: FIXED SCOPE WIDENED: chat reply budget hardcoded to 100 in the frontend while the user-configurable GenerationConfig.max_new_tokens is consumed by ZERO server sites (Settings control is dead)
